business_glossary_term: Asset Contract Coverage - Asset Contract Coverage Id
description: Primary key for the asset_contract_coverage association
Foreign key linking to the mining equipment asset covered under this contract

business_glossary_term: Asset Contract Coverage - Procurement Contract Id
description: Foreign key linking to the procurement contract providing coverage for this asset
Date when this asset was formally added to the contract coverage. Used for audit trail and amendment tracking.
Annualized monetary value of coverage for this specific asset under this contract. Used for cost allocation, budget tracking, and contract value analysis.
Date when contract coverage expires for this specific asset. Used to trigger renewal processes and prevent coverage gaps.
Free-text notes capturing special conditions, exclusions, or requirements specific to this asset-contract coverage (e.g., 'Excludes tire replacement', 'Requires monthly inspection report').
Date when contract coverage becomes effective for this specific asset. May differ from the master contract start date if assets are added mid-term.

Current status of the coverage relationship: active (in force), suspended (temporarily paused), expired (coverage period ended), pending activation (scheduled future start), or cancelled (terminated early).

Type of service coverage provided under this contract for this asset: full maintenance (parts and labor), parts supply only, labor only, preventive maintenance only, breakdown support only, telematics monitoring, or warranty extension.
Number of service labor hours included in the coverage for this asset during the coverage period. Nullable if coverage is parts-only or unlimited hours.
Date when this asset was removed from contract coverage (if applicable). Nullable for currently covered assets.
Contractually committed maximum response time in hours for service calls on this asset. Used for SLA compliance monitoring and vendor performance measurement.
SLA tier or service level commitment applicable to this asset under this contract (e.g., gold, silver, bronze). Defines priority, response times, and service scope.
Unique identifier for each asset-stakeholder concern record. Primary key for the association.
Foreign key linking to the specific mining asset that is the subject of stakeholder concern or engagement
Foreign key linking to the community stakeholder who has raised concerns or requires engagement regarding the asset
Classification of the type of concern or impact the stakeholder has regarding this specific asset. Identified in detection phase relationship data.
Free-text description of the specific concern this stakeholder has about this asset, including context and stakeholder perspective.
Date when the stakeholder first raised this concern about the asset. Establishes the timeline for the concern relationship.
Date when the concern was formally resolved to the stakeholder's satisfaction, if applicable.
Required frequency of engagement with this stakeholder specifically about this asset, based on concern severity and stakeholder expectations. Identified in detection phase relationship data.
Current escalation status of the concern indicating urgency and management attention required. Identified in detection phase relationship data.
Indicates whether the stakeholder has lodged a formal grievance through the grievance mechanism regarding this asset.
Reference number of the formal grievance lodged regarding this asset-stakeholder concern, if applicable.
Indicates whether a formal impact assessment has been completed for this asset-stakeholder concern combination.
Date of the most recent engagement activity specifically regarding this asset-stakeholder concern. Identified in detection phase relationship data.
Description of specific mitigation actions implemented or planned to address this stakeholder concern about this asset.
Current status of mitigation measures implemented to address the stakeholder concern about this asset. Identified in detection phase relationship data.
Scheduled date for the next engagement activity with this stakeholder regarding this specific asset concern.
Additional notes and context regarding the asset-stakeholder concern relationship, engagement history, and stakeholder feedback.
Name or employee ID of the community relations officer responsible for managing this specific asset-stakeholder concern.
Primary key for equipment_shutdown_scope
Foreign key linking to the specific mining asset included in this shutdown scope
Reference to another shutdown_scope record that must be completed before work on this asset can commence, establishing sequencing dependencies within the shutdown critical path
Identifier of the maintenance supervisor or foreman accountable for coordinating and completing work on this asset during the shutdown
Foreign key linking to the planned maintenance shutdown event
Unique identifier for this asset-shutdown scope record
Actual duration in hours that this asset was unavailable during shutdown execution, measured from isolation to return-to-service
Actual total cost incurred for work on this asset during shutdown execution, aggregated from work orders and purchase orders
Actual total labour hours consumed for work on this asset during shutdown execution, captured from timesheets and work orders
Criticality classification indicating whether this asset is on the shutdown critical path, near-critical (within float tolerance), or non-critical for overall shutdown duration
Current lifecycle status of this asset within the shutdown workflow, tracking progression through readiness gates from pre-shutdown preparation to return-to-service
Priority classification for this asset within the shutdown scope, indicating urgency and resource allocation precedence
Percentage completion of work on this asset, used for shutdown progress tracking and earned value analysis
Current completion status of work on this asset within the shutdown, tracking whether work is complete, in progress, or deferred to a future shutdown
Estimated total cost for work on this asset including labour, materials, and contractor services, contributing to total shutdown cost
Estimated total labour hours required to complete work on this asset during the shutdown, used for resource planning and cost estimation
Date and time when this asset was formally isolated and locked out for shutdown work, marking the start of asset-specific downtime
Free-text notes capturing issues, delays, scope changes, or other relevant information specific to this asset's participation in the shutdown
Estimated duration in hours that this specific asset will be unavailable during the shutdown, used for production loss calculations and resource planning
Date when post-shutdown commissioning and performance testing was completed, authorizing return-to-service
Indicates whether this asset requires formal commissioning and performance testing before being returned to operational service after shutdown work completion
Date when the pre-shutdown inspection was completed for this asset, establishing baseline condition and confirming scope
Indicates whether this asset requires a formal pre-shutdown inspection to assess condition and finalize work scope before shutdown commencement
Date and time when this asset was returned to operational service after shutdown work completion and commissioning, marking the end of asset-specific downtime
Business identifier for the scope item within the shutdown, used for work package tracking and communication (e.g., SD2024-001, SD2024-002)
Sequencing order for this asset within the shutdown critical path, indicating when work on this asset should commence relative to other assets (e.g., crusher must be down before feeder work starts)
Primary trade or craft skill required for work on this asset (e.g., mechanical fitter, electrician, boilermaker, millwright), used for resource leveling
Detailed description of the maintenance work to be performed on this asset during the shutdown, including specific tasks, inspections, and repairs

Unique surrogate identifier for each equipment inspection record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete, lifecycle-managed business event (pre-start or periodic inspection) with regulatory standing.
reference: Infor EAM; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Reference to the equipment asset (haul truck, drill, shovel, conveyor, processing plant unit, etc.) that was inspected. Links to the equipment master register sourced from Infor EAM and Caterpillar MineStar. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE / MASTER_RESOURCE category.

Foreign key linking to project.capital_project. Business justification: Pre-commissioning and commissioning inspections are project deliverables and handover requirements. Business process: handover certification, acceptance testing, and punch list closure require linking

Reference to the versioned checklist template applied during this inspection, specific to the equipment class (e.g., haul truck pre-start checklist v3.2). Ensures traceability of which checklist version was in force at the time of inspection.
reference: IsoMetrix; Infor EAM; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Foreign key linking to hse.corrective_action. Business justification: Failed equipment inspections generate corrective actions to remediate defects and prevent recurrence. This is a core compliance workflow in mining safety management systems. Inspectors must track that

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Inspection costs (labor, materials) are allocated to cost centres for maintenance budget tracking and compliance cost reporting in mining operations.

business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Incident ID
description: Reference to an associated HSE incident record in IsoMetrix if this inspection was triggered by or linked to a safety incident (e.g., post-incident inspection). Null for routine pre-start and periodic inspections.

Reference to the supervisor who reviewed and approved the inspection record. Required for statutory and post-incident inspections. Null for self-certified pre-start inspections where supervisor sign-off is not mandated.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Reference to the workforce record of the person who conducted the inspection (operator, maintainer, or supervisor). Used for competency verification and regulatory accountability. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Self-referencing FK on inspection (previous_inspection_id)

Foreign key linking to hse.risk_assessment. Business justification: Equipment inspections identify hazards (worn components, safety system failures, structural defects) that feed into risk assessments. Inspection findings directly inform residual risk ratings and cont
Reference to the mine site or operational location where the inspection was conducted. Supports site-level compliance reporting and regulatory submissions per jurisdiction.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Reference to the corrective maintenance work order generated in Infor EAM as a result of defect findings identified during this inspection. Null if no corrective action was required or work order has not yet been raised.
Date and time when the supervising officer approved the inspection record. Null if not yet approved or approval not required. Supports regulatory audit trails for statutory inspections.

Number of checklist items that were assessed and recorded during this inspection. A value less than checklist_items_total may indicate an incomplete inspection, which is a compliance risk for pre-start and statutory inspections.
reference: IsoMetrix; Infor EAM; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Total number of checklist items included in the inspection for this equipment class and inspection type. Used to calculate completion rate and to validate that all mandatory items were assessed.
reference: IsoMetrix; Infor EAM; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Indicates whether one or more defect findings from this inspection require a corrective action to be raised. True triggers work order generation in Infor EAM and/or a corrective action task in IsoMetrix. Critical for HSE compliance workflow integration.
reference: IsoMetrix; Infor EAM; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Timestamp when this inspection record was first created in the source system. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

Number of checklist items rated as critical severity during this inspection. Critical defects require immediate equipment shutdown and corrective action before operation can resume. A value greater than zero should result in a fail overall result.

Number of checklist items rated as major severity during this inspection. Major defects require corrective action within a defined timeframe but may allow conditional operation under specified controls.
Number of checklist items rated as minor severity during this inspection. Minor defects are recorded for monitoring and scheduled maintenance but do not prevent equipment operation.

Date and time when the inspector completed and submitted the inspection. Used to calculate inspection duration and to confirm the inspection was completed before equipment operation commenced (pre-start compliance).

Classification of the equipment type being inspected. Determines which checklist template applies and which regulatory requirements govern the inspection. Sourced from the equipment master register in Infor EAM and Caterpillar MineStar. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: haul_truck|drill|shovel|excavator|dozer|grader|conveyor|crusher|processing_plant|light_vehicle — promote to reference product]
reference: Infor EAM; Caterpillar MineStar; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Indicates whether the equipment was taken out of service (grounded) as a result of this inspection. True means the equipment must not be operated until corrective action is completed and a return-to-service inspection is passed. Directly impacts fleet availability and OEE calculations.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001; Caterpillar MineStar; Infor EAM

description: Engine or operating hours recorded on the equipment at the time of inspection. Used to determine whether periodic maintenance-based inspections are due and to track equipment utilisation context at the time of the inspection. Sourced from Caterpillar MineStar telematics.
reference: Infor EAM; Caterpillar MineStar; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Human-readable fleet number or asset tag of the equipment being inspected (e.g., HT-042, DR-007). Denormalized from the equipment master for operational convenience and to support inspection records even when the equipment master FK is temporarily unavailable.

Method by which the inspection was captured and submitted. Mobile app refers to field-based digital capture. Paper form indicates a manual record subsequently digitised. Desktop portal is a web-based entry. Integrated OBC (on-board computer) refers to direct capture from Caterpillar MineStar on-board systems.

Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the inspection record as assigned by the source system (IsoMetrix or Infor EAM). Used for cross-system reference, regulatory submissions, and audit trails. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
reference: Infor EAM; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001

description: Current workflow state of the inspection record. Draft indicates the inspection is in progress or not yet submitted. Submitted means the inspector has completed and lodged the record. Approved indicates supervisor sign-off. Rejected means the record was returned for correction. Cancelled applies to inspections that were voided. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.

Classification of the inspection by its regulatory or operational trigger. Pre-start inspections are legally mandated before equipment operation in most mining jurisdictions. Periodic inspections occur at scheduled intervals. Post-incident inspections follow a safety event. Statutory inspections are required by specific mining regulations. Return-to-service inspections occur after maintenance or repair.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001; WHS Act (Australia); IsoMetrix

description: Free-text narrative comments provided by the inspector to describe defect findings, operational context, or observations not captured by the structured checklist items. Supports incident investigation and root cause analysis.

Competency or certification code held by the inspector that authorises them to conduct this class of inspection (e.g., operator licence number, statutory inspector certificate). Required for regulatory compliance verification. Sourced from SAP HR competency records.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001; WHS Act (Australia)

description: Role of the person conducting the inspection. Operators conduct pre-start checks. Maintainers conduct post-maintenance checks. Supervisors conduct periodic and statutory inspections. Statutory inspectors are government-appointed or certified inspectors. Third-party inspectors are external contractors.

Free-text description of the specific location within the mine site where the inspection was conducted (e.g., ROM pad, pit level 3, crusher feed area). Supplements the site_id with operational granularity for incident investigation and compliance reporting.

Odometer reading in kilometres recorded at the time of inspection, applicable to mobile equipment such as haul trucks and light vehicles. Null for fixed plant and equipment without odometers. Supports distance-based maintenance scheduling.

Aggregate pass/fail outcome of the inspection. Pass indicates all checklist items met the required standard. Fail indicates one or more critical or major defects were found that prevent safe operation. Conditional pass indicates minor defects noted but equipment may operate under specified conditions pending corrective action.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001; IsoMetrix; Infor EAM

description: Number of photographic evidence items attached to this inspection record to document defect findings. Supports regulatory audit requirements and insurance claims. Photos are stored in the document management system with references captured at the checklist item level.

The specific mining safety regulation or standard under which this inspection is mandated or conducted. Enables jurisdiction-specific compliance reporting and regulatory submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MSHA_30CFR56|MSHA_30CFR57|WHS_ACT|DMIRS_WA|MINES_ACT_QLD|ISO_45001 — promote to reference product]
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57; ISO 45001; WHS Act (Australia); ICMM

description: The shift during which the inspection was conducted. Pre-start inspections are typically conducted at the commencement of each shift. Used for shift-level compliance reporting and to correlate inspection outcomes with shift patterns.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; IsoMetrix; MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this inspection record was ingested into the lakehouse silver layer. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and troubleshooting of ETL pipelines.

The native primary key or record identifier of this inspection in the originating source system (IsoMetrix, Infor EAM, or mobile app). Enables back-referencing to the source system for reconciliation and audit purposes.

Date and time when the inspector commenced the inspection. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category. Critical for regulatory compliance — pre-start inspections must be completed before equipment operation commences.

Timestamp when this inspection record was last modified in the source system. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Tracks amendments, supervisor approvals, and corrective action updates.
Primary key for inspection_checklist
Self-referencing FK on inspection_checklist (parent_inspection_checklist_id)
Comma-separated list of shift types during which this inspection checklist must be executed, such as day shift, night shift, or all shifts.
Comma-separated list of mine site codes where this inspection checklist is applicable and must be used.
Role or position title of the authority responsible for approving changes to this inspection checklist.
Username or identifier of the authority who approved this inspection checklist version for operational use.
Timestamp when this inspection checklist version was formally approved for operational use.
Timestamp when this inspection checklist was archived and removed from active operational use.
Externally-known unique business identifier for the inspection checklist used across systems and documentation.
Detailed description of the inspection checklist including its objectives, scope, and application context.
Human-readable name of the inspection checklist describing its purpose and scope.
Classification of the inspection checklist by its operational purpose and timing in the asset lifecycle.
Version number of the inspection checklist following semantic versioning to track revisions and updates.
Username or identifier of the user who created this inspection checklist record.
Timestamp when this inspection checklist record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether a digital or mobile-enabled form is available for executing this inspection checklist in the field.
Date from which this inspection checklist version becomes valid and mandatory for use in operations.
Date until which this inspection checklist version remains valid; nullable for currently active checklists without planned retirement.
Category of mining equipment or asset that this checklist applies to, aligned with fleet and plant classifications.
Expected time in minutes required to complete the full inspection checklist under normal conditions.
Required frequency at which this inspection checklist must be executed to maintain compliance and operational standards.
Username or identifier of the user who last modified this inspection checklist record.
Timestamp when this inspection checklist record was last modified or updated.
Date when this inspection checklist was last formally reviewed for accuracy, relevance, and compliance.
Number of checkpoints within this checklist that are mandatory and must be completed for the inspection to be considered valid.
Indicates whether this inspection checklist is compatible with mobile applications used by field operators and maintenance personnel.
Scheduled date for the next formal review of this inspection checklist to ensure continued relevance and compliance.
Additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to the execution or governance of this inspection checklist.
Business department or functional area responsible for maintaining and governing this inspection checklist.
Minimum percentage of checkpoints that must pass for the overall inspection to be considered successful and the asset to be cleared for operation.
Indicates whether photographic evidence must be captured and attached during execution of this inspection checklist.
Indicates whether this inspection checklist is mandated by regulatory or statutory requirements versus being operationally discretionary.
Minimum competency or qualification level required for personnel authorized to execute this inspection checklist.
Indicates whether completion of this inspection checklist requires formal certification or sign-off by a qualified inspector or supervisor.
Required interval in months between formal reviews of this inspection checklist to maintain governance standards.
Indicates whether this inspection checklist addresses safety-critical systems or conditions that could result in harm if not properly inspected.
Operational system of record from which this inspection checklist definition originates or is maintained.
Current lifecycle status of the inspection checklist indicating its availability for operational use.
Total number of individual inspection checkpoints or items included in this checklist.
Unique surrogate identifier for each physical mining asset record in the master register. Primary key for the asset data product.

Foreign key linking to equipment.asset_class. Business justification: The asset table currently stores asset_class as a STRING attribute, but a dedicated asset_class master table exists with PK asset_class_id. This is a classic denormalization pattern that should be nor

Foreign key linking to project.capital_project. Business justification: Mining equipment assets are acquired and commissioned within capital projects (mine expansions, new processing plants). Business process: asset capitalization tracking, project asset registers, and ha

Reference to the parent asset in a multi-component asset hierarchy (e.g., an engine assembly belonging to a haul truck). Enables parent-child asset relationship modelling for complex equipment units. Null for top-level assets.

Foreign key linking to hse.ppe_issuance. Business justification: Certain equipment requires specialized PPE (hearing protection for drill rigs, fall protection for elevated platforms, respiratory protection for enclosed cabs). Asset records should link to the PPE i

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Mining equipment has OEM suppliers; tracking vendor enables warranty claims, parts procurement, and supplier performance analysis. Real business process: OEM parts sourcing and warranty management. Ne

Foreign key linking to project.project_contract. Business justification: Equipment procurement contracts (haul trucks, excavators, processing equipment) are managed as project contracts. Business process: equipment supply agreement tracking, warranty management, and contra

Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Mining assets are often dedicated to specific product streams (iron ore haul trucks, coal handling equipment). Production planning, asset allocation, and performance reporting require tracking which p

Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Mining equipment operates within specific tenement boundaries. Real operations track which licence area each asset is deployed to for regulatory compliance, expenditure allocation, and operational pla

Foreign key linking to hse.training_record. Business justification: Specific equipment classes require operator certification (haul truck licenses, dozer tickets, drill rig competencies). Assets should reference the required training/competency record to enforce that

Original capital expenditure (CAPEX) purchase price of the asset in the reporting currency. Used for depreciation calculations, asset register valuation, and capital replacement planning under IAS 16 and IFRS.
Human-readable descriptive name of the asset, typically combining equipment type and fleet number (e.g., 'Haul Truck HT-042', 'SAG Mill 01'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and work orders.

Date the asset was formally commissioned and placed into operational service at the mine site. Marks the start of the asset's operational lifecycle for maintenance scheduling, warranty tracking, and depreciation under IFRS.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle; IFRS 16; IAS 16

description: SAP S/4HANA cost center code to which the asset's operating expenditure (OPEX) and maintenance costs are allocated. Enables financial reporting by asset and supports OPEX tracking against budget.

Maintenance criticality classification of the asset based on its impact on production, safety, and environmental compliance if it fails. Drives maintenance strategy selection, spare parts stocking levels, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) prioritisation.
reference: Infor EAM Criticality Analysis; ISO 55001 Asset Management; ICMM

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the acquisition cost and financial values associated with the asset (e.g., AUD, USD, ZAR). Supports multi-currency asset register reporting.

Date the asset was permanently removed from operational service and decommissioned. Null for assets still in service. Used for asset lifecycle reporting, capital replacement planning, and mine rehabilitation cost estimation.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle; IFRS 16; IAS 16

description: Source system identifier for the asset record in Infor EAM. Used for system-of-record traceability and integration with maintenance work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, and asset lifecycle management.

OEM-rated engine or motor power output of the asset in kilowatts (kW). Used for fuel consumption benchmarking, energy efficiency analysis, and equipment selection for mine planning. Null for non-powered assets.

Operational fleet number assigned to the asset at the mine site. Used by operators, dispatchers, and Fleet Management System (FMS) to identify and track the asset in the field. Sourced from Caterpillar MineStar and Infor EAM.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Master; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

description: Maximum fuel tank capacity of the asset in litres. Used for fuel logistics planning, refuelling scheduling, and fuel consumption rate benchmarking. Null for electric or non-fuel-powered assets.
Primary energy source or fuel type powering the asset. Used for fuel consumption tracking, emissions reporting under GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement, and fleet electrification planning.
reference: GRI 305 Emissions; ISO 14001; IsoMetrix Environmental Monitoring

description: Indicates whether the asset is a mobile mining unit (True) such as a haul truck, excavator, or drill rig, or a fixed plant asset (False) such as a conveyor, crusher, or mill. Drives different tracking, reporting, and maintenance workflows.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Classification; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

description: Date of the most recent major overhaul or rebuild performed on the asset. Used to assess remaining component life, plan future overhauls, and calculate Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) in the maintenance management system.
reference: Infor EAM Work Order History; ICMM Asset Management Guidelines

description: Descriptive operational location of the asset within the mine site (e.g., 'Pit 3 North Wall', 'Processing Plant - Grinding Circuit', 'ROM Pad'). Complements the site code with granular positional context for maintenance and dispatch.
reference: Infor EAM Location Hierarchy; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

description: Calendar year in which the asset was manufactured by the OEM. Used to calculate asset age, depreciation schedules, and Life of Mine (LOM) planning for fleet replacement.
OEM model designation of the asset (e.g., CAT 793F, Komatsu 930E, Sandvik DR461i). Used for spare parts management, maintenance procedures, and performance benchmarking against OEM specifications.
Date of the next planned preventive maintenance service for the asset as scheduled in Infor EAM. Used for maintenance planning, production scheduling, and availability forecasting.

Current cumulative odometer reading in kilometres for mobile assets. Used alongside SMR hours for maintenance scheduling, tyre life management, and haul road condition monitoring. Null for fixed plant assets.
reference: Infor EAM PM Scheduling; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

description: OEM-rated operating weight of the asset in metric tonnes. Used for road and haul route load limit compliance, ground bearing pressure calculations, and mine infrastructure design.

Current operational lifecycle status of the asset indicating whether it is available for production, undergoing maintenance, on standby, or permanently decommissioned. Drives availability calculations and maintenance scheduling in Infor EAM and MineStar.

Indicates whether the asset is company-owned, leased under a finance or operating lease, short-term hired, or contractor-supplied. Drives financial treatment under IFRS 16 and determines maintenance responsibility.

OEM-rated maximum payload capacity of the asset in metric tonnes. Applicable to haul trucks, loaders, and material handling equipment. Used for production planning, haulage cycle optimisation, and OEE calculations. Null for fixed plant assets.
Timestamp when the asset record was first created in the master register. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and compliance with asset register governance requirements.
Timestamp when the asset record was most recently updated in the master register. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and integration refresh management in the Databricks Silver Layer.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Tag
description: SCADA tag identifier used to link the asset to its real-time process data streams in the OSIsoft PI System historian. Applicable primarily to fixed plant assets such as conveyors, crushers, mills, and processing equipment.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SCADA Integration Standards

description: Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) serial number uniquely identifying the physical asset unit. Used for warranty tracking, OEM service records, and regulatory compliance. Sourced from Infor EAM.

Code identifying the mine site where the asset is currently assigned and operated. Enables site-level fleet reporting, OEE benchmarking, and cross-site asset utilisation analysis. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA Plant Master.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Plant Master; Infor EAM Location

description: Current cumulative Service Meter Reading (SMR) in engine hours recorded on the asset. Used as the primary trigger for preventive maintenance scheduling, component life tracking, and MTBF calculations in Infor EAM.
reference: Infor EAM PM Scheduling; Caterpillar MineStar Equipment Health

description: Internal asset tag or barcode label affixed to the physical asset for inventory and maintenance identification. Distinct from fleet number and serial number. Sourced from Infor EAM.

Identifier of the onboard telematics or GPS tracking unit installed on the asset. Used to link real-time positional and operational data from Caterpillar MineStar and OSIsoft PI System for fleet management and equipment health monitoring.
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; OSIsoft PI System

description: OEM-specified or engineering-assessed useful operational life of the asset in years. Used for straight-line depreciation calculations, Life of Mine (LOM) fleet planning, and capital replacement scheduling under IAS 16.
reference: IAS 16; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; Infor EAM

description: Date on which the OEM warranty for the asset expires. Used to trigger warranty claim processes, plan post-warranty maintenance strategies, and manage OEM service agreements in Infor EAM and Pronto Xi.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Master; Pronto Xi Procurement

description: SAP Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element associated with the asset for capital expenditure (CAPEX) tracking and project cost allocation. Used for mine development and capital project reporting.
Unique surrogate identifier for each asset class record in the mining equipment classification hierarchy. Primary key for the asset_class reference master.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Classification; SAP S/4HANA PM Equipment Category

description: Expected useful life of the asset class expressed in calendar years for financial depreciation and LOM planning purposes. Used alongside useful_life_operating_hours to determine the binding depreciation constraint. Supports CAPEX modelling and NPV/IRR analysis.
reference: IAS 16 Property Plant and Equipment; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; IFRS Capital Budgeting Standards

description: Unit of measure for the nominal_capacity field (e.g., t for payload tonnes, t/h for throughput tonnes per hour, m3 for bucket/bowl volume, mm for drill hole diameter, kW for power rating). Ensures correct interpretation of capacity values across equipment types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: t|t/h|m3|m3/h|mm|kW|MW|m|km/h — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ISO 80000-1 Quantities and Units; Infor EAM Unit of Measure; SAP S/4HANA Unit of Measure

description: Capital expenditure (CAPEX) budget category under which assets of this class are typically funded. Sustaining CAPEX covers replacement of existing capacity; expansion CAPEX covers new capacity additions. Used for capital allocation, LOM planning, and financial reporting under IFRS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-IM Capital Investment Management; IFRS Capital Expenditure Classification; ICMM Financial Reporting

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the asset class within the equipment classification hierarchy (e.g., HT-320T for 320-tonne haul truck class, SAG-36FT for 36-foot SAG mill class). Used as the business key across ERP, EAM, and FMS systems.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Class Code; SAP S/4HANA PM Asset Class (ANLKL); Caterpillar MineStar Equipment Class

description: Detailed narrative description of the asset class including its primary function, operational context within the mine, and key distinguishing characteristics. Supports procurement specifications and capital budgeting documentation.

Human-readable name of the asset class describing the equipment type and key specification (e.g., 'Ultra-Class Haul Truck 320T', 'Semi-Autogenous Grinding Mill 36ft', 'Rotary Blasthole Drill 270mm'). Used in reports, dashboards, and maintenance planning documents.
reference: Infor EAM; Caterpillar MineStar Fleet Classification

description: Current lifecycle status of the asset class record. Active classes are in current use for fleet planning and procurement. Phasing_out classes are being replaced by newer models. Retired classes are no longer procured but may still have operating assets. Controls visibility in procurement and planning systems.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle; SAP S/4HANA PM; ISO 55001 Asset Management

description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) emission factor for assets of this class in kilograms per operating hour, derived from OEM fuel consumption specifications and applicable emission conversion factors. Used for Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions reporting under GRI, ICMM, and regulatory environmental disclosure requirements.
reference: GRI 305 Emissions; ICMM Environmental Reporting; ISO 14001 Environmental Management; IsoMetrix Environmental Monitoring

description: Timestamp when this asset class record was first created in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Provides audit trail for data governance and lineage tracking in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time; Data Governance Audit Trail Standards

description: Free-text field for production supervisors or engineers to record contextual notes about this OEE record, such as reasons for low availability, abnormal operating conditions, or data quality caveats.

description: The ratio of actual production speed to ideal production speed during operating time, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8750 = 87.50%). Second component of the OEE composite metric. description: The exact date and time marking the end of the production period for which OEE is calculated. Combined with period_start_timestamp to derive total period duration.

description: Calendar date associated with this OEE record, representing the production day. Used for daily and monthly OEE trend reporting and OPEX period alignment.

description: Current lifecycle status of this OEE record within the production reconciliation workflow. Draft records are provisional; approved records are used for OPEX reporting and fleet benchmarking.
reference: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; Infor EAM

description: Number of production units that did not meet quality specification during the period (e.g., crusher throughput below grade spec, off-spec concentrate batches). reference: LabWare LIMS Quality Control; OSIsoft PI System; ISO 22400-2

description: Planned or budgeted throughput in dry metric tonnes for this asset during the period. Used for production variance analysis and OEE Performance Rate benchmarking against mine plan.

description: Unit of measure for the assay result. Must match expected_grade_unit for valid comparison. Percent (%) for major elements, parts per million (ppm) for trace elements, grams per tonne (g/t) for precious metals.
reference: LabWare LIMS Unit Standards; SI Units and Mining Industry Standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the entire sample batch must be reanalyzed due to systematic QA/QC failure (e.g., multiple CRM failures, blank contamination, duplicate precision failure). True triggers batch rejection and resubmission workflow.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: Calculated percentage difference between assay_result and expected_grade, expressed as ((assay_result - expected_grade) / expected_grade) * 100. Positive values indicate over-reporting, negative values indicate under-reporting. Used to assess laboratory accuracy and systematic error.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Statistical Quality Control Methods

description: Certified standard deviation for CRM samples as documented in the supplier certificate. Null for non-CRM QA/QC sample types. Used to calculate statistical control limits and assess laboratory precision against certified variability.
reference: CRM Certificate Documentation; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or context regarding this QA/QC sample (e.g., sample handling issues, laboratory comments, unusual results). Supports audit trails and knowledge capture.
reference: LabWare LIMS Sample Comments; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

description: Timestamp when this QA/QC sample record was first created in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

Lower detection limit of the analytical method for the target analyte, expressed in the same unit as assay_result. Results below this value are typically reported as less-than (<) values. Critical for blank sample evaluation.
reference: LabWare LIMS Method Detection Limits; ISO/IEC 17025

description: Certified or expected assay grade for the QA/QC sample, expressed in the same unit as the target analyte (e.g., % for iron ore, ppm for gold, g/t for precious metals). For CRMs, this is the certified value; for blanks, this is typically zero or below detection limit; for duplicates, this is the original sample grade.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; NI 43-101 Section 11; CRM Certificate Documentation

description: Unit of measure for the expected grade value. Percent (%) for major elements, parts per million (ppm) for trace elements, grams per tonne (g/t) for precious metals, ounces per ton (oz/t) for imperial systems, milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg) for environmental samples.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; SI Units and Mining Industry Standards

description: Target insertion frequency of this QA/QC sample type expressed as a percentage of total samples (e.g., 5.00 means 1 in 20 samples). Used to validate compliance with QA/QC protocols and JORC/NI 43-101 requirements.

Sequential position of the QA/QC sample within the batch submission stream. Used to verify insertion frequency and systematic placement per QA/QC protocols (e.g., 1 CRM per 20 samples, 1 blank per 40 samples).
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: Free-text field documenting investigation findings, root cause analysis, and corrective actions taken for failed QA/QC samples. Null if no investigation required. Critical for audit trails and continuous improvement.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; ISO/IEC 17025 Corrective Action Requirements

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this QA/QC result requires formal investigation due to failure, systematic bias, or contamination. True triggers investigation workflow per JORC/NI 43-101 requirements.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: External job or work order number assigned by the laboratory for this batch submission. Used for cross-referencing with laboratory certificates and invoices.
reference: LabWare LIMS External Reference; Laboratory Certificate Documentation

description: Timestamp when this QA/QC sample record was last modified in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for audit trails and change tracking.

Sample preparation technique applied before analysis (e.g., crush_to_minus_2mm, pulverize_to_85pct_minus_75um, dry_at_105c, digest_four_acid). Critical for duplicate QA/QC samples to ensure preparation consistency.
reference: LabWare LIMS Preparation Protocols; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Number
description: Externally-known unique identifier for the QA/QC sample, typically following laboratory naming conventions (e.g., CRM-2023-001, BLK-001, DUP-045). Used for sample tracking and audit trails.
reference: LabWare LIMS Sample Numbering; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Type
description: Classification of the QA/QC control sample type. Certified Reference Material (CRM) validates accuracy, blanks detect contamination, field duplicates assess sampling precision, pulp duplicates assess analytical precision, coarse duplicates assess crushing/splitting precision, and standards validate instrument calibration.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3 - QA/QC Procedures; NI 43-101 Section 11; SAMREC Code 2016

description: Pass/fail status of the QA/QC sample based on comparison of assay_result against tolerance limits. Pass indicates result within acceptable range, fail triggers investigation and potential batch rejection, warning indicates borderline result, pending awaits analysis, not_analyzed indicates sample not yet processed.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: Date the QA/QC sample was submitted to the laboratory as part of the batch. Used for turnaround time tracking and temporal QA/QC trend analysis.
reference: LabWare LIMS Submission Tracking; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

description: Lower acceptable limit for assay results, typically defined as expected_grade minus acceptable variance (e.g., 2 standard deviations for CRMs, detection limit for blanks). Results below this threshold trigger QA/QC failure flags and investigation.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: Method used to define tolerance limits. Absolute uses fixed grade units, relative_percent uses percentage of expected grade, standard_deviation uses statistical variance from certified mean. Determines how tolerance_lower and tolerance_upper are calculated.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Statistical Quality Control Methods

description: Upper acceptable limit for assay results, typically defined as expected_grade plus acceptable variance (e.g., 2 standard deviations for CRMs, maximum contamination threshold for blanks). Results above this threshold trigger QA/QC failure flags and investigation.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

description: Total approved design capacity of the waste dump expressed in Bank Cubic Metres (BCM). Represents the maximum volume of in-situ material the facility is permitted and engineered to receive. Sourced from mine planning systems (Hexagon MinePlan, Deswik).
reference: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; JORC Code 2012; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Total approved design capacity of the waste dump expressed in dry metric tonnes. Complements BCM capacity for mass-balance reconciliation and LOM planning. Sourced from mine planning systems.
reference: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; LOM Planning Standards

description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the waste dump facility, used in mine planning systems (Hexagon MinePlan, Deswik) and regulatory submissions. Unique across the mine site.
Human-readable name assigned to the waste dump facility (e.g., 'North Waste Dump 1', 'Southern Overburden Emplacement'). Used in operational communications, mine plans, and regulatory reports.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ICMM Tailings and Waste Management Guidelines

description: Current lifecycle status of the waste dump facility. Active indicates ongoing waste emplacement; closed indicates emplacement has ceased; rehabilitating indicates progressive or final rehabilitation is underway per the mine closure plan.
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; IsoMetrix HSE Module

description: Classification of the waste dump by material type deposited. Overburden refers to material above the ore body; waste rock is non-economic mineralised material; low-grade stockpile holds sub-cut-off-grade ore for potential future processing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overburden|waste_rock|low_grade_stockpile|mixed|tailings_co_disposal — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
reference: JORC Code 2012; ICMM Waste Management Guidelines

description: Elevation of the waste dump crest above mean sea level in metres. Critical for geotechnical stability assessment, drainage design, and regulatory height limit compliance.
reference: Geotechnical Engineering Standards; ISO 14001; Mine Design Standards

description: Geotechnical risk classification of the waste dump based on foundation conditions, material properties, and consequence of failure. Class 1 (lowest risk) to Class 4 (highest risk). Drives inspection frequency, monitoring requirements, and regulatory reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: class_1|class_2|class_3|class_4 — promote to reference product]
reference: ANCOLD Guidelines; Geotechnical Engineering Standards; ISO 14001

description: Indicates whether ongoing groundwater quality monitoring is required for this waste dump as a condition of the environmental permit or based on ARD risk classification. True triggers monitoring schedule in IsoMetrix.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions; IsoMetrix Environmental Module

description: Source system identifier for this waste dump facility as recorded in IsoMetrix HSE and Environmental Monitoring module. Used for data lineage and cross-system reconciliation.
Date of the most recent topographic survey conducted on the waste dump to update volume and surface area measurements. Survey data is used to reconcile FMS haulage records with actual fill volumes.
reference: Mine Survey Standards; Hexagon MinePlan Survey Module

description: Geographic latitude of the waste dump centroid or reference point in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for GIS mapping, environmental monitoring zone delineation, and regulatory spatial reporting.
reference: GIS Standard WGS84; ISO 14001; EIS Spatial Reporting

description: Current operational status of the leachate collection and management system for the waste dump. Indicates whether leachate is being actively collected, passively monitored, or not required based on liner type and regulatory conditions.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions; IsoMetrix Environmental Module

description: Type of engineered liner system installed at the base of the waste dump to control leachate migration and protect groundwater. None indicates an unlined facility; HDPE geomembrane is a high-density polyethylene synthetic liner. Sourced from mine design records and IsoMetrix.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions; IsoMetrix Environmental Module

description: Geographic longitude of the waste dump centroid or reference point in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for GIS mapping, environmental monitoring zone delineation, and regulatory spatial reporting.
reference: GIS Standard WGS84; ISO 14001; EIS Spatial Reporting

description: Maximum permitted or current height of the waste dump from base to crest in metres. A key geotechnical design parameter governing slope stability and regulatory permit conditions.
reference: Geotechnical Engineering Standards; Mine Permit Conditions; ICMM

description: Source system identifier for this waste dump as recorded in the mine planning system (Hexagon MinePlan or Deswik). Used for data lineage, cross-system reconciliation, and LOM schedule integration.
Date of the next scheduled geotechnical or environmental inspection of the waste dump as required by the geotechnical classification, permit conditions, or IsoMetrix inspection schedule.
reference: ISO 14001; ISO 45001; IsoMetrix HSE Module; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Free-text field for operational notes, geotechnical observations, or special conditions applicable to this waste dump that are not captured in structured fields. Used by mine planning and environmental teams.
Designed overall slope angle of the waste dump in degrees from horizontal. A critical geotechnical stability parameter reviewed against factor-of-safety thresholds in the geotechnical design report.
reference: Geotechnical Engineering Standards; ICMM Slope Stability Guidelines

description: Date on which the environmental permit or licence for this waste dump expires and must be renewed. Triggers compliance workflow in IsoMetrix for permit renewal actions.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions; IsoMetrix Environmental Module

description: Regulatory permit or licence number issued by the relevant environmental authority authorising the construction and operation of this waste dump. Required for compliance tracking and regulatory reporting.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions; IsoMetrix Environmental Module

description: Cumulative area of the waste dump that has been progressively rehabilitated to date, expressed in hectares. Used to track rehabilitation progress against permit commitments and LOM closure plan milestones.
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Indicates whether progressive rehabilitation (rehabilitation of completed dump benches during the operational phase) is required as a permit condition or company commitment. True drives progressive rehab scheduling in the LOM plan.
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Timestamp when this waste dump master record was first created in the data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001 Record Keeping

description: Timestamp when this waste dump master record was most recently updated in the data platform. Used for change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001 Record Keeping

description: Financial assurance (bond) amount in the site's functional currency held by the relevant regulatory authority to cover the estimated cost of rehabilitating this waste dump to an approved post-mining land use standard. Commercially sensitive.
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; IFRS 6; Mine Permit Conditions

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the rehabilitation bond amount (e.g., AUD, USD, ZAR). Required for multi-jurisdiction financial reporting under IFRS.
reference: ISO 4217; IFRS 6; ICMM Mine Closure Framework

description: Document reference number or identifier for the approved mine rehabilitation and closure plan applicable to this waste dump. Links to the formal closure plan document registered in the document management system. Required for regulatory compliance and bond calculation.
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Mine Closure Framework; EIS; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Name or employee identifier of the qualified geotechnical engineer responsible for the design, monitoring, and sign-off of this waste dump facility. Required for regulatory accountability and competent person declarations.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ISO 45001; Mine Permit Conditions

description: Total surface footprint of the waste dump facility in hectares, including all active and inactive benches. Used for rehabilitation cost estimation, environmental bond calculation, and land tenure management.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS; Mine Rehabilitation Bond Calculation Standards

description: Geochemical classification of the predominant waste rock material deposited in the dump based on laboratory acid-base accounting. Non-Acid Forming (NAF), Potentially Acid Forming (PAF), or Acid Forming (AF). Determines encapsulation and placement strategy.
reference: INAP ARD Guidelines; LabWare LIMS; ISO 14001; EIS

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the grade control block record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS Block Model Standards

description: Foreign key linking to mine.bench. Business justification: grade_control_block has bench_name (STRING) and bench_elevation_m (DECIMAL) but no FK to bench table. Adding bench_id FK normalizes bench reference and removes redundant name and elevation columns. Th

Foreign key linking to geology.block_model_cell. Business justification: Grade control blocks are derived from block model cells for operational execution. Essential for linking short-term mine plans to long-term resource models and tracking model accuracy.

Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Grade control blocks are classified by geological domain for estimation consistency. Critical for applying correct grade estimation parameters and ensuring operational classification matches resource

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample Batch ID
description: Identifier of the assay sample batch in LabWare LIMS from which the grade data for this block was sourced. Provides traceability from the grade control block back to the laboratory analysis records.
reference: LabWare LIMS Sample Management; ISO/IEC 17025 Laboratory Accreditation

description: Reference identifier linking this grade control block to the corresponding mining block or polygon in the mine planning system (Hexagon MinePlan or Deswik). Enables reconciliation between grade control and mine plan.

Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Grade control blocks are spatial subdivisions of orebodies for operational ore/waste classification. Critical for dispatch decisions, dilution tracking, and production reconciliation against orebody m

Foreign key linking to mine.pit_or_level. Business justification: grade_control_block has pit_name (STRING) but no FK to pit_or_level table. Adding pit_or_level_id FK normalizes pit/level reference and removes redundant name column. The pit_or_level table contains n

Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Grade control blocks are classified and dispatched according to production schedule. N:1 relationship (many blocks per schedule). No bidirectional conflict. Valid operational link.

Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Grade control blocks are sampled within prospect boundaries. Grade control programs reference exploration prospect geology for classification, dispatch decisions, and ore/waste designation. Essential

Identifier of the geological resource block model version from which this grade control block's initial grade estimates were derived. Enables traceability back to the JORC-compliant resource model in Geovia GEMS.
reference: Geovia GEMS Resource Model; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101

description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Grade control blocks are dispatched to specific product destinations (lump, fines, different grade products). Critical operational decision linking mine execution to product specifications. Ore_type_c

Identifier of the drill-and-blast pattern associated with this grade control block. Links the block to the blast design from which grade control samples were collected. Used for blast-to-mill reconciliation.
reference: Hexagon MinePlan Blast Design; Drill and Blast SOP

description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Grade control blocks must be attributed to tenements for accurate reserve depletion reporting, royalty calculations on mined ore grades, and compliance with mining lease resource extraction conditions
Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the grade control block as assigned in Geovia GEMS or the mine's block model system. Used for cross-system traceability and field reference.
reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model; JORC Code 2012 Section 1

description: Human-readable name or label assigned to the grade control block, typically combining bench, row, and column identifiers for operational reference at the mine face.
reference: Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan Grade Control Module

description: Horizontal dimension of the grade control block in the X (easting) direction, in metres. Defines the block geometry used for volume and tonnage calculations.
reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model Specification; JORC Code 2012

description: Horizontal dimension of the grade control block in the Y (northing) direction, in metres. Defines the block geometry used for volume and tonnage calculations.
reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model Specification; JORC Code 2012

description: Vertical dimension (height) of the grade control block in metres, typically equal to the bench height. Used for volume and tonnage calculations.
reference: Geovia GEMS Block Model Specification; Mine Planning Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the grade control block indicating its operational state. 'active' = classified and awaiting dispatch; 'dispatched' = ore/waste destination assigned; 'mined_out' = block fully extracted; 'on_hold' = pending re-assay or review; 'cancelled' = block voided.
Calculated volume of the grade control block in cubic metres, derived from block dimensions. Used as the basis for in-situ tonnage estimation.
reference: Geovia GEMS; JORC Code 2012 Resource Estimation

description: Bulk density of the material in the grade control block expressed in tonnes per cubic metre (t/m³). Used to convert block volume to in-situ tonnes. Sourced from laboratory measurements or geological domain defaults.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Item 14; LabWare LIMS Density Measurements

description: Easting coordinate of the block centroid in the mine's local or projected coordinate system (metres). Used for spatial location, blast pattern design, and GIS integration.
reference: GIS Standards; Geovia GEMS Spatial Reference; Mine Survey SOP

description: Northing coordinate of the block centroid in the mine's local or projected coordinate system (metres). Used for spatial location, blast pattern design, and GIS integration.
reference: GIS Standards; Geovia GEMS Spatial Reference; Mine Survey SOP

description: Grade control classification of the block based on cut-off grade analysis. Determines whether the block is directed to the mill, ROM pad, low-grade stockpile, or waste dump. This is the primary ore/waste discrimination decision for the block.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 2; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Cut-off Grade Methodology

description: Date on which the ore/waste classification decision was made for this grade control block, based on assay results and cut-off grade analysis. Represents the principal business event date for this entity.
reference: Mine Operations SOP; Grade Control Procedure

description: Confidence level assigned to the grade estimate for this block, reflecting the density and quality of sampling data. 'high' = well-drilled with close-spaced samples; 'medium' = adequate sampling; 'low' = sparse data, interpolated grade. Influences dispatch decision risk.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 2 (Measured/Indicated/Inferred analogue for grade control); CIM Definition Standards

description: Timestamp when this grade control block record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation marker for data lineage and compliance purposes.
reference: ISO 8601; Data Governance Audit Trail Standards; IFRS 6

description: The minimum economic grade threshold applied to classify this block as ore or waste. Blocks with primary_grade at or above this value are classified as ore. Derived from the current LOM (Life of Mine) economic parameters and commodity price assumptions.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 2; CIM Definition Standards; Mine Economics SOP

description: Estimated percentage of waste or gangue material mixed with ore during mining of this block, expressed as a percentage. Dilution reduces the effective grade of mined material relative to in-situ grade. Used for reconciliation and production planning.
reference: Mine Planning SOP; JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Item 16; Dilution Control Standards

description: Date on which the dispatch instruction was issued and material from this grade control block was directed to its assigned destination. Used for production scheduling reconciliation and haulage tracking.
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; Mine Production Reporting SOP

description: Assigned destination for the material in this grade control block based on its classification. Drives truck dispatch instructions in the Fleet Management System (FMS). 'mill_feed' = direct to processing plant; 'rom_pad' = Run of Mine stockpile; 'low_grade_stockpile' = future processing; 'waste_dump' = permanent waste; 'tsf' = Tailings Storage Facility.
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS Dispatch; Mine Operations SOP; ROM Pad Management Procedure

description: Specific dispatch instruction code issued to the Fleet Management System (FMS) for truck routing of material from this block. Corresponds to a destination code in Caterpillar MineStar for automated truck assignment.
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; Mine Dispatch SOP

description: Statistical or geostatistical method used to estimate the grade of this block from drill hole or blast hole assay data. Common methods include Ordinary Kriging, Inverse Distance Weighting, and Nearest Neighbour.
reference: Geovia GEMS Estimation Module; JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Item 22; CIM Geostatistics Guidelines

description: Estimated in-situ dry metric tonnes of material within the grade control block, calculated from block volume and bulk density. Represents the raw tonnage before mining dilution or recovery adjustments.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Section 2; CIM Definition Standards; Geovia GEMS

description: Indicates whether this grade control block has been subject to a re-assay or resampling event due to initial classification uncertainty or grade variability. True = block was resampled; False = original assay used. Supports audit trail for classification decisions.
reference: LabWare LIMS; Grade Control QA/QC SOP; ISO/IEC 17025

description: Date on which the grade control block was fully extracted and the block status transitioned to 'mined_out'. Used for production reconciliation, LOM tracking, and mine closure planning.
reference: Mine Production Reporting SOP; LOM Planning Standards

description: Geological domain or mineralisation zone code to which this block belongs, as defined in the resource model. Used for grade estimation and variogram modelling within homogeneous geological units.
reference: Geovia GEMS Geological Domain Model; JORC Code 2012 Table 1

description: Assay-derived grade of the primary commodity (e.g., Fe%, Cu%, Li ppm) for the grade control block. The principal quantitative fact driving ore/waste classification and dispatch decisions. Units depend on commodity (% for Fe/Cu, ppm for Li/Au).
reference: LabWare LIMS Assay Results; JORC Code 2012 Table 1; ISO 11536 (Iron Ore Analysis)

business_glossary_term: Primary Commodity Grade Unit of Measure
description: Unit of measure for the primary commodity grade value (e.g., 'pct' for percentage, 'ppm' for parts per million, 'g_per_t' for grams per tonne). Ensures correct interpretation of the primary_grade field across different commodities.
Estimated percentage of the primary commodity that will be recovered during mineral processing of this block's material. Used for contained metal calculations and production forecasting.
reference: Metallurgical Recovery Model; JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Item 17; Mine Planning SOP

description: Number of drill hole or blast hole assay samples used in the grade estimation for this block. Higher sample counts generally indicate greater confidence in the grade estimate.
reference: LabWare LIMS Sample Management; JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Item 20

description: Assay-derived grade of a secondary or by-product commodity (e.g., SiO2%, Al2O3%, S%) for the grade control block. Used for penalty/bonus calculations, blending decisions, and metallurgical planning.
reference: LabWare LIMS Assay Results; JORC Code 2012 Table 1

description: Chemical element or compound symbol for the secondary grade value (e.g., 'SiO2', 'Al2O3', 'S', 'P'). Identifies which element the secondary_grade field represents for this block.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to this grade control block record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: ISO 8601; Data Governance Audit Trail Standards; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Life of Mine (LOM) plan record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to community.benefit_sharing_agreement. Business justification: LOM revenue projections drive benefit-sharing calculations (royalty percentages, trust fund contributions, infrastructure commitments). Agreement terms are embedded in mine planning assumptions. Real

Foreign key linking to project.capital_project. Business justification: LOM plans are mandatory technical inputs for capital project approval (stage gates, feasibility studies). Every major mining capital project (pit expansion, underground development, processing plant)

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: LOM plans are budgeted and tracked against specific cost centres for financial planning, AISC reporting, and operational cost allocation. Standard mining finance structure for life-of-mine cost manage

Foreign key linking to hse.environmental_permit. Business justification: Life-of-mine plans must reference the primary environmental permit authorizing mining operations. Regulatory requirement for demonstrating operations are within permitted scope and conditions.

Foreign key linking to hse.legal_register. Business justification: LOM plans must demonstrate compliance with applicable mining and environmental legislation. Links plan to legal compliance framework for regulatory reporting and competent person sign-off.

Foreign key linking to mine.mine_site. Business justification: Life of Mine plans are specific to mine sites. Adding mine_site_id FK establishes the site context for the plan. The lom_plan table has warehouse_location_id but no direct mine_site reference, which i

Foreign key linking to exploration.ore_reserve. Business justification: LOM plans extract ore reserves that define the economically extractable portion of resources. Reserve declarations are the basis for LOM production scheduling, financial modeling, and regulatory repor

Foreign key linking to finance.profit_centre. Business justification: LOM plans roll up to profit centres for segment reporting, NPV analysis, corporate financial consolidation, and JORC reserve reporting. Core mining finance hierarchy for profitability tracking.

Foreign key linking to finance.project_valuation. Business justification: LOM plans are valued via project valuation studies for NPV, IRR, investment decision-making, and reserve reporting. Core valuation link for mining project economics.

Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Life-of-Mine plans are built on prospects that have been converted to reserves. LOM planning requires traceability to the original exploration prospect for resource classification, regulatory reportin
