Foreign key linking to geology.resource_statement. Business justification: LOM plans are based on resource statements as the foundation for reserve conversion. Required for regulatory compliance, investor reporting, and linking mine plans to competent person declarations.

Foreign key linking to community.social_impact_assessment. Business justification: Life-of-mine plans are developed to address SIA findings and regulatory conditions. SIA commitments constrain mine planning (resettlement timing, heritage exclusions, benefit-sharing obligations). Req

Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: LOM plans must reference the primary tenement for JORC/NI 43-101 reserve reporting, regulatory submissions, and legal mining authority verification. Essential for competent person sign-off and ASX/SEC

All-In Sustaining Cost (AISC) per tonne, expressed in USD. Includes C1 cash costs plus sustaining CAPEX, royalties, and corporate G&A. Provides a comprehensive cost measure for economic viability assessment and investor disclosure.
reference: World Gold Council AISC Standard 2018; ICMM; SEC S-K 1300

description: The date on which this LOM plan version received formal executive or board approval. Marks the transition from 'under_review' to 'approved' status and triggers downstream planning and budgeting activities.
reference: JORC Code 2012; SEC S-K 1300; SAP S/4HANA PS project governance

description: Name or employee identifier of the executive or technical authority who formally approved this LOM plan version. Required for governance, audit trail, and regulatory compliance.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001; ICMM governance framework; SAP S/4HANA PS

description: The average annual ore extraction rate in million tonnes per year (Mtpa) over the full LOM plan. Used for steady-state OPEX modelling, workforce planning, and long-term supply agreements.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Deswik production scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan

description: The average head grade of the ore reserve included in the LOM plan, expressed in the same unit as cutoff_grade_unit. A key input to revenue and concentrate production forecasts.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; Geovia GEMS resource estimation

description: The C1 Cash Cost per tonne of ore or concentrate produced, expressed in USD. Represents direct cash costs of mining and processing excluding royalties, depreciation, and sustaining capital. Industry-standard cost metric for benchmarking and investor reporting.
reference: World Gold Council Cost Reporting Standard; ICMM; Brook Hunt C1 methodology

description: The primary mineral commodity targeted by this LOM plan (e.g., iron_ore, copper, lithium). Drives cut-off grade assumptions, processing routes, and commodity price inputs used in NPV/IRR calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iron_ore|copper|coal|lithium|nickel|gold|zinc|bauxite|manganese|silver|other — promote to reference product]

The long-term commodity price assumption used in the LOM financial model, expressed in USD per tonne (or per lb/oz as applicable). A critical sensitivity input; changes to this assumption materially affect NPV and IRR outcomes.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: Name of the Competent Person (JORC/SAMREC) or Qualified Person (NI 43-101/SEC S-K 1300) who has reviewed and signed off on the mineral resource and reserve estimates underpinning this LOM plan. Required for regulatory disclosure.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101 Section 1.1; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300

description: The timestamp when this LOM plan record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse audit standards; ICMM data governance

description: The minimum economic grade of ore included in the LOM plan reserve, below which material is classified as waste. Expressed in the commodity-appropriate unit (e.g., % Fe for iron ore, % Cu for copper, g/t Au for gold). Drives ore/waste classification and reserve estimation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: Unit of measure for the cut-off grade value (e.g., 'pct' for percentage Fe/Cu, 'g_per_t' for grams per tonne Au/Ag, 'ppm' for parts per million). Required to correctly interpret the cutoff_grade field.

The real or nominal discount rate (%) applied in the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model to calculate the NPV of the LOM plan. Typically represents the Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) or a project-specific hurdle rate.
reference: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: The foreign exchange rate assumption used in the LOM financial model (e.g., AUD/USD, CLP/USD). Applied to convert local currency OPEX and CAPEX to USD for NPV/IRR calculations. A key sensitivity variable in the financial model.
reference: IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI; SEC S-K 1300

description: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of the LOM plan expressed as a percentage. The discount rate at which the NPV of the project equals zero. Used alongside NPV as a primary investment hurdle metric for project sanctioning.
reference: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: The overall Life of Mine strip ratio, expressed as tonnes of waste per tonne of ore (t:t). A key economic indicator representing the ratio of overburden to ore that must be moved to extract the ore reserve. Calculated as total_waste_mt / total_ore_reserve_mt.
reference: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Deswik scheduling

description: Total planned duration of the mine life in years, from first ore extraction to final closure. Derived from plan_start_date and plan_end_date for planning purposes; stored explicitly for reporting and regulatory disclosure.

Primary mining method employed in this LOM plan. 'open_cut' refers to open-pit operations; 'underground' includes methods such as Sub-Level Caving (SLC) and longwall; 'open_cut_underground' indicates a combined operation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Deswik method classification

description: Net Present Value (NPV) of the LOM plan in millions of USD, calculated using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) methodology at the specified discount rate. Primary financial metric for investment decision-making and project approval.
reference: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014; ICMM

description: The maximum planned annual ore extraction rate in million tonnes per year (Mtpa) over the LOM plan. Used for infrastructure sizing, processing plant capacity planning, and peak CAPEX determination.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Deswik production scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan

description: Externally-known business identifier for the LOM plan, typically assigned by the mine planning team in Deswik or Hexagon MinePlan. Format: LOM-{SITE}-{YEAR}. Used for cross-system referencing and regulatory submissions.
reference: JORC Code 2012; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

business_glossary_term: Life of Mine (LOM) Plan End Date
description: The calendar date on which the LOM plan production schedule concludes, representing the projected end of mine life including rehabilitation and closure activities.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001; Mine Rehabilitation and Closure standards

description: Human-readable name of the LOM plan (e.g., 'Pilbara Iron Ore LOM 2024 Base Case'). Used for identification in planning reports and executive dashboards.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Hexagon MinePlan naming conventions

business_glossary_term: Life of Mine (LOM) Plan Start Date
description: The calendar date from which the LOM plan production schedule commences. Represents the effective start of the planned mine life, aligned with the first scheduled ore extraction period.

Current lifecycle status of the LOM plan. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' indicates pending technical and executive sign-off; 'approved' is the active SSOT plan; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'archived' indicates retired from active use.
reference: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; ISO 14001

description: Classification of the LOM plan scenario. 'base_case' is the primary planning scenario; 'upside_case' and 'downside_case' represent sensitivity scenarios; 'closure_case' models mine rehabilitation; 'feasibility' is used for pre-production studies.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: Version identifier of the LOM plan (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.3'). Enables tracking of iterative revisions and scenario comparisons over the mine life planning cycle.
reference: Deswik LOM versioning conventions; Hexagon MinePlan

description: The planned metallurgical recovery rate expressed as a percentage, representing the proportion of the valuable mineral extracted from the ore during processing. A critical input to concentrate production and revenue forecasting in the LOM plan.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; Mineral Processing and Beneficiation standards

description: Probable Ore Reserve category in million tonnes, as defined by JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC. Lower geological confidence than Proved Reserve but still economically viable and included in the LOM production schedule.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; IFRS 6

description: Highest-confidence ore reserve category (Proved Reserve) in million tonnes, as defined by JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC. Represents the portion of the ore body with the greatest geological certainty, used in bankable feasibility studies and investor disclosures.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; IFRS 6

description: The mineral resource and reserve reporting standard under which this LOM plan has been prepared and disclosed (e.g., JORC for Australia, NI 43-101 for Canada, SAMREC for South Africa, SEC S-K 1300 for US-listed companies).
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

description: The highest mineral resource classification category underpinning the LOM plan per JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC standards. 'measured' is highest confidence, 'indicated' is moderate, 'inferred' is lowest. Determines the regulatory disclosure obligations for the plan.

description: The total planned drilling metres for blast hole drilling associated with this schedule period. A key drill-and-blast planning metric used to size drilling equipment requirements and schedule blast events.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; Drilling and Blasting Operations Standards

description: The planned number of truck haulage cycles required to move the scheduled ore and waste tonnes during the period. Used for fleet utilisation planning and fuel consumption estimation in the Fleet Management System (FMS).
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; Deswik Mine Planning

description: The planned Operating Expenditure (OPEX) in USD associated with executing this production schedule for the period. Includes mining, haulage, and processing costs. Used for budget tracking and AISC (All-In Sustaining Cost) reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO; OPEX (Operating Expenditure) Standard; AISC (All-In Sustaining Cost) Standard; IFRS

description: The scheduled quantity of ore (in dry metric tonnes) to be extracted from the mining block or stope during the schedule period. Represents the primary production target and is the principal quantitative fact of this schedule record. Excludes waste and overburden.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: The planned percentage of the valuable mineral expected to be recovered from the ore during mineral processing and beneficiation. Expressed as a percentage. Drives concentrate production targets and revenue forecasting.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Recovery Rate (Percentage of Valuable Mineral Extracted) Standard; JORC Code 2012

description: The planned ratio of waste tonnes to ore tonnes (waste:ore) for the schedule period. A key economic indicator in open-cut mining used to assess mining cost efficiency. Calculated as planned_waste_tonnes / planned_ore_tonnes but stored as a scheduled target value from the mine plan.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; Strip Ratio (Overburden to Ore Ratio) Standard

description: Total planned material movement (ore plus waste, in dry metric tonnes) for the schedule period. Used for equipment allocation, fleet sizing, and haulage planning via the Fleet Management System (FMS).
reference: Caterpillar MineStar FMS; Deswik Mine Planning

description: The scheduled quantity of waste rock and overburden (in dry metric tonnes) to be moved during the schedule period. Used to calculate the planned strip ratio and assess haulage and equipment requirements.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; Strip Ratio Standards

description: The JORC/CIM resource or reserve classification of the ore scheduled for extraction. Values align with JORC Code categories: 'measured' (Measured Resource), 'indicated' (Indicated Resource), 'inferred' (Inferred Resource), 'probable_reserve' (Probable Reserve), 'proved_reserve' (Proved Reserve — highest confidence).
reference: JORC Code 2012; CIM NI 43-101; SAMREC; SEC S-K 1300

description: Indicates the planning basis of this schedule record. 'budget' is the approved annual plan; 'forecast' is a revised in-period estimate; 'actual_reconciled' is a schedule updated with actual production data; 'scenario' is a what-if planning scenario.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO; Deswik Mine Planning; ICMM Reporting Standards

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this production schedule record as sourced from Deswik or Hexagon MinePlan (e.g., PS-2024-Q3-001). Used for cross-system reference and operational reporting.
Human-readable descriptive name for the production schedule (e.g., 'North Pit Q3 2024 Monthly Schedule'). Used for identification in planning dashboards and operational reports.

Current lifecycle state of the production schedule. 'draft' indicates under preparation; 'approved' indicates sign-off by mine planning; 'active' indicates currently being executed; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a revised version; 'cancelled' indicates no longer valid.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: Temporal horizon classification of the schedule. 'weekly' covers 7-day operational targets; 'monthly' covers 4-week periods; 'quarterly' covers 13-week periods; 'annual' covers full-year plans; 'lom' refers to Life of Mine (LOM) long-range planning schedules.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; LOM (Life of Mine) Planning Standards

description: Incremental version number of the production schedule, incremented each time the schedule is revised and re-approved. Enables tracking of schedule revisions and comparison between versions for variance analysis.

Identifies the operational system of record from which this production schedule record was sourced. 'DESWIK' indicates Deswik mine planning software; 'HEXAGON_MINEPLAN' indicates Hexagon MinePlan; 'MANUAL' indicates a manually entered schedule.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning; Hexagon MinePlan; Data Lineage Standards

description: The planned average grade of the primary commodity (e.g., % Fe for iron ore, % Cu for copper, g/t Au for gold) in the ore scheduled for extraction. Expressed as a decimal fraction or percentage per commodity convention. Drives mill feed quality targets and recovery rate planning.
reference: Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012; Cut-off Grade Standards

description: The date and time when this production schedule record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing.

reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

reference: SAP S/4HANA PS; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

Foreign key linking to mine.lom_plan. Business justification: Stope designs are part of the overall LOM plan. N:1 relationship (many stope designs in one LOM plan). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link.

Reference to the mine planning block or stope envelope from which this design was derived. Links to the block model and resource estimation data in Geovia GEMS.
reference: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; Deswik Mine Planning

description: Reference to the geological orebody or mineralised zone that this stope design targets. Links to the geological resource model for grade, tonnage, and resource classification context.
reference: Geovia GEMS Geological Modeling; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101

description: Foreign key linking to mine.mine_plan_scenario. Business justification: Stope designs can be generated from mine plan scenarios. N:1 relationship (many stope designs from one scenario). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link.

Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Underground stope designs target specific prospects discovered during exploration. Mine engineers reference prospect geology, mineralization style, and structural characteristics when designing extrac

Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Underground stope designs must remain within tenement boundaries for legal compliance. Critical for resource classification reporting and ensuring extraction rights are valid for designed ore bodies.

Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Underground stope designs are developed under capital projects for development capex tracking, engineering cost control, and underground project cost management. Capital project link for underground m

Foreign key linking to geology.wireframe. Business justification: Stope designs are bounded by orebody wireframes for extraction planning. Required for underground design, ensuring stopes remain within ore boundaries, and dilution control.
Name or employee identifier of the authorised engineer or geotechnical specialist who formally approved this stope design for construction issue.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001; Deswik Stope Optimization

description: Date on which the stope design was formally approved by the authorised geotechnical or mine planning engineer, permitting issue for construction. Null if not yet approved.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

description: Specified minimum unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of the cemented backfill in megapascals (MPa) at the design cure time. Applicable only to cemented paste fill and cemented rock fill designs. Drives cement binder content and backfill plant mix design.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

description: Type of backfill material specified for this stope design after ore extraction. Determines geotechnical stability of adjacent stopes, backfill plant requirements, and extraction sequence constraints. None indicates open stoping without backfill.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

description: Timestamp when this stope design record was first created in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

Minimum economic grade threshold applied to define the stope boundary and determine ore versus waste classification within the design. Expressed in the same unit as design_grade_primary. Directly impacts designed ore tonnes and LOM economics.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards; SAMREC Code

description: Date on which the current revision of the stope design was formally completed and issued by the mine design engineer.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Estimated in-situ grade of the primary commodity within the designed stope boundary, expressed in the commodity-appropriate unit (g/t for gold/silver, % for base metals). Derived from the block model and used for mill feed planning and revenue forecasting.
reference: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC Code

description: Sequential revision number of the stope design, incremented each time the design is formally updated. Revision 0 represents the initial issue; subsequent revisions capture engineering changes, geotechnical updates, or grade re-interpretations.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; ISO 19650 Information Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the stope design record, tracking progression from initial draft through engineering review, approval, and construction issue. Superseded status indicates a newer revision has replaced this design.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; ISO 19650 Information Management

description: Name or employee identifier of the mine design engineer responsible for authoring this stope design revision.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Planned dilution percentage representing the proportion of waste rock expected to be extracted with the ore due to stope geometry and mining method. Expressed as a percentage of total ROM tonnes. Key input to mill feed grade forecasting.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

description: Estimated in-situ ore tonnage within the designed stope boundary, calculated from the block model grade-tonnage curve. Represents the planned ore extraction quantity before dilution and recovery adjustments.
reference: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards

description: Planned ore recovery percentage representing the proportion of in-situ ore tonnes expected to be extracted from the stope. Accounts for ore loss to pillars, hangingwall slough, and extraction method limitations.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

description: Total designed void volume of the stope in cubic metres as calculated from the 3D stope solid in Deswik or Geovia GEMS. Used for backfill volume estimation, blast design, and ventilation requirements.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Native stope identifier from the Deswik mine planning and stope optimisation system. Enables reconciliation between the silver layer data product and the Deswik source system for scheduling and optimisation workflows.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling

description: Underground mining extraction method applied to this stope design. Determines drill pattern, blast design, support requirements, and backfill strategy. Key driver of dilution, recovery rate, and OPEX. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: longhole_open|longhole_retreat|cut_and_fill|sublevel_caving|sublevel_stoping|bench_and_fill|room_and_pillar|shrinkage — promote to reference product]
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

description: Planned extraction sequence number of this stope within its mining block or production area. Governs the order of stope firing to manage geotechnical stability, backfill curing time, and ventilation circuit integrity.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Native stope object identifier from the Geovia GEMS geological modelling and mine design system. Used for traceability and data lineage between the silver layer data product and the source system of record.
reference: Geovia GEMS Mine Design; SAP S/4HANA PS

description: Unit of measure for the primary commodity grade value (e.g., g/t for gold, % for copper or iron ore, ppm for trace elements). Ensures correct interpretation of design_grade_primary across different commodity types.

Geotechnical ground support classification assigned to the stope design, typically based on rock mass rating (RMR) or Q-system. Drives the specification of rock bolts, cable bolts, mesh, and shotcrete requirements. Class A = competent rock; Class E = very poor ground.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001; Deswik Stope Optimization

description: Elevation in metres above mean sea level (mAMSL) of the primary extraction level or ore drive floor for this stope design. Used for ventilation circuit design, dewatering planning, and LOM scheduling.
reference: Geovia GEMS Mine Design; Deswik Mine Planning; GIS Coordinate Reference Systems

description: Life of Mine (LOM) planning period or fiscal year-quarter in which this stope is scheduled for extraction (e.g., 'FY2026-Q2'). Links the stope design to the LOM production schedule in Deswik for NPV and IRR modelling.
reference: Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling; SAP S/4HANA CO; IFRS 6 Exploration

description: Number of ore drives (extraction drives) designed within the stope footprint. Determines development metres required, drill rig access, and mucking logistics for the stope.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Designed height of each ore drive (extraction drive) within the stope in metres. Determines equipment clearance and development cost per metre.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Designed width of each ore drive (extraction drive) within the stope in metres. Determines equipment clearance, drill pattern geometry, and development cost per metre.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Type of geotechnical pillar incorporated into the stope design to maintain ground stability. Crown pillars separate stopes vertically; rib pillars separate stopes horizontally; sill pillars provide floor support; barrier pillars protect major infrastructure. None indicates pillarless design.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

description: Designed width of the geotechnical pillar in metres. Null if no pillar is specified (pillar_type = none). Critical geotechnical parameter determining pillar stability factor and ore loss to pillars.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

description: Principal mineral commodity targeted by this stope design. Determines processing route, grade control requirements, and commodity-specific regulatory reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iron_ore|copper|coal|lithium|nickel|gold|zinc|lead|silver|manganese|cobalt — promote to reference product]
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC Code; SEC S-K 1300

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the stope design within the mine planning system. Used as the primary business reference across Deswik, Geovia GEMS, and SAP PS work breakdown structures.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design; SAP PS Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

description: Designed vertical height of the stope from floor to back (crown) in metres. Critical input for geotechnical stability assessment, cable bolt design, and blast energy calculations.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57

description: Designed horizontal length of the stope along the strike direction in metres. Primary dimension used for volume calculation, drill pattern design, and production scheduling.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Human-readable name or label assigned to the stope design, typically incorporating level, drive, and sequence identifiers (e.g., 'L15-OD-001'). Used in engineering drawings, P&IDs, and operational communications.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Designed horizontal width of the stope across the orebody in metres. Determines minimum mining width, dilution exposure, and equipment access requirements.
reference: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

description: Vertical distance in metres between sublevels within the stope design, applicable to sublevel caving (SLC) and sublevel stoping extraction methods. Drives drill ring burden, blast design, and ore recovery modelling.

Timestamp when this stope design record was most recently modified in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Tracks design revision history and supports change management auditing.

business_glossary_term: Ventilation Airflow Requirement (cubic metres per second)
description: Minimum required fresh air supply to the stope in cubic metres per second (m³/s) during active extraction, as specified in the stope design. Determined by diesel equipment fleet, blast fume clearance time, and regulatory minimum airflow standards.
reference: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57 Ventilation; ISO 45001; Deswik Mine Planning

description: Narrative summary of the optimal operating conditions identified from this beneficiation test, including recommended grind size, reagent dosages, pH, density, and temperature. Directly informs circuit design parameters and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; NI 43-101 Section 13; Internal Metallurgical Testwork Procedure

description: Percentage of the target commodity recovered from the feed into the product stream during the beneficiation test. Primary performance indicator for metallurgical testwork; informs LOM plan recovery assumptions.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; NI 43-101 Section 13; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Document reference number or URL for the formal metallurgical testwork report associated with this test. Provides traceability to the full technical report for audit, regulatory disclosure, and competent person review.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101 Section 13; SEC S-K 1300; ISO/IEC 17025

description: Total mass of the ore sample (in kilograms) used as feed for the beneficiation test. Determines the representativeness of the test and the reliability of mass balance calculations.

Descriptive reference to the origin of the ore sample used in the test, including mine site, pit, bench, drill hole, or stockpile location. Provides traceability for the sample provenance as required by JORC and NI 43-101.
Grade of the target commodity remaining in the tailings stream after beneficiation, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess metal losses and validate mass balance closure.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Operating temperature in degrees Celsius during the beneficiation test. Particularly relevant for leaching (heap leach, pressure oxidation), SX-EW, and bio-leach tests where temperature significantly affects reaction kinetics and recovery.
reference: SME Mineral Processing Handbook; OSIsoft PI System Process Historian

description: The date on which the beneficiation test was conducted. Principal real-world event date for this testwork record.
Total duration of the beneficiation test in minutes, from feed introduction to final product collection. Used to calculate throughput rates and assess residence time requirements for circuit design.
reference: LabWare LIMS; Internal Metallurgical Testwork Procedure

description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned by the laboratory or pilot plant (e.g., LabWare LIMS test ID) to uniquely identify this testwork trial. Used for cross-referencing with laboratory reports and LIMS records.

Statement of the specific metallurgical objective for this test (e.g., 'Determine optimal collector dosage for copper flotation', 'Assess leach kinetics for oxide ore at 60°C'). Provides context for interpreting results and linking to LOM plan requirements.
reference: Internal Metallurgical Testwork Procedure; JORC Code 2012

description: Narrative summary of the key findings and outcomes of the beneficiation test, including notable observations, anomalies, and conclusions. Supports metallurgical reporting and competent person review.
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; NI 43-101 Section 13; CIM Definition Standards

description: Scale at which the beneficiation test was conducted, distinguishing between bench-scale laboratory tests, locked-cycle tests, batch tests, and pilot plant trials. Determines the confidence level and applicability of results to full-scale circuit design.
Current lifecycle status of the beneficiation test. Tracks progression from planning through execution to completion or cancellation.

Classification of the beneficiation or metallurgical testwork method applied. Includes flotation, leach, gravity separation, Dense Media Separation (DMS), magnetic separation, Solvent Extraction Electrowinning (SX-EW), High Pressure Grinding Rolls (HPGR), and comminution tests. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flotation|leach|gravity|DMS|magnetic_separation|SX-EW|HPGR|comminution|bio_leach|roasting — promote to reference product]
reference: JORC Code 2012 Table 1; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Total mass of all reagents consumed per tonne of feed processed during the beneficiation test, expressed in kg/t. Used for operating cost estimation and OPEX modelling in LOM plan updates.
reference: SME Mineral Processing Handbook; Internal OPEX Estimation Standard

description: Timestamp when this beneficiation test record was last modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and incremental data load processes.

Ratio of product grade to feed grade, indicating the degree of concentration achieved in the beneficiation test. A higher upgrade ratio indicates more effective separation of the valuable mineral from gangue.
reference: SME Mineral Processing Handbook; JORC Code 2012

description: Volume of water consumed per tonne of feed processed during the beneficiation test, expressed in m³/t. Informs water balance modelling and environmental impact assessments for circuit design.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement; Internal Water Management Standard

description: Unique surrogate identifier for this circuit-method protocol assignment record

business_glossary_term: Circuit Analytical Protocol - Analytical Method Id
description: Foreign key linking to the approved analytical method used for this circuit

business_glossary_term: Circuit Analytical Protocol - Processing Circuit Id
description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit for which this analytical protocol is defined
Business or technical rationale for selecting this analytical method for this circuit (e.g., detection limit requirements, matrix compatibility, accreditation needs)
Name or identifier of the technical authority (metallurgist, process engineer, or laboratory manager) who approved this method for this circuit
Percentage of this circuit's analytical budget allocated to this specific method, used for cost tracking and budget forecasting
Date from which this circuit-method protocol became active and operational
Date on which this circuit-method protocol was superseded or retired. Null for currently active protocols.
Date on which this analytical method was formally approved for use on this processing circuit by the technical authority
Priority classification of this method for this circuit (primary for routine use, secondary for confirmation, backup for contingency, research for trials)
Current operational status of this circuit-method protocol assignment
Required frequency of quality control sample insertion for this circuit-method combination, expressed as percentage (e.g., 5.00 means one QC sample per 20 production samples)
Required number of samples to be collected and analyzed using this method per operating shift for this circuit
Maximum allowable turnaround time from sample submission to result reporting for this circuit-method combination, driven by process control requirements
Unique surrogate identifier for each circuit-asset assignment record
Foreign key linking to the physical asset assigned to the circuit

business_glossary_term: Circuit Asset Assignment - Processing Circuit Id
description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit to which the asset is assigned
Current operational status of the assignment indicating whether the asset is actively operating in the circuit, temporarily inactive, under maintenance, or being reconfigured.

Specific position or location code of the asset within the circuit flowsheet (e.g., PRIMARY_MILL_1, ROUGHER_CELL_3, CYCLONE_BANK_A). Used for circuit configuration management and maintenance work order routing.

Operational duty classification of the asset within the circuit indicating whether it operates as primary equipment, secondary/parallel unit, or standby/backup capacity. Drives maintenance prioritization and availability calculations.
Date on which the asset was physically installed and commissioned into the processing circuit. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and performance period calculation.

Cumulative operating hours logged by the asset while assigned to this specific circuit. Used for circuit-specific maintenance scheduling and performance analysis. Distinct from the asset's total SMR hours across all assignments.

Percentage contribution of this asset to the overall circuit throughput or recovery performance. Used for metallurgical accounting, bottleneck analysis, and asset performance attribution in multi-unit circuits.
Date on which the asset was removed from the processing circuit due to maintenance, reconfiguration, or decommissioning. Null indicates the asset is currently assigned.
Unique surrogate identifier for this circuit delivery record, serving as the primary key for the association between a capital project and a processing circuit
Foreign key linking to the capital project responsible for delivering this processing circuit
Foreign key linking to the processing circuit being delivered by this capital project
Actual capital expenditure incurred to deliver this specific processing circuit as part of the broader capital project. Used for cost tracking and variance analysis at circuit level.
Date on which this specific processing circuit was commissioned as part of this capital project. Marks the formal acceptance of the circuit into operational testing phase.

Duration in months of the defects liability period during which the project team or contractor remains responsible for rectifying defects in the delivered circuit. Typically 12-24 months from provisional acceptance.
Free-text field capturing key observations, issues, lessons learned, or special conditions related to the delivery of this circuit by this project
Boolean indicator of whether the delivered processing circuit achieved its nameplate design capacity during performance testing. Used to track project delivery success and trigger milestone payments.
Date on which the processing circuit received final acceptance after successful completion of the defects liability period, formally closing out the project delivery obligation

Current lifecycle status of the circuit handover process from the project team to operations. Tracks progression through construction, commissioning, testing, acceptance, and defects liability phases.
Date on which performance acceptance testing was conducted for this circuit delivery to verify that design throughput, recovery rates, and other KPIs meet contractual specifications
Date on which the processing circuit was provisionally accepted by operations, marking the start of the defects liability period and transfer of operational responsibility
Unique surrogate identifier for each circuit-product configuration record. Primary key for the association.

business_glossary_term: Circuit Product Configuration - Processing Circuit Id
description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit that is configured to produce the saleable product

business_glossary_term: Circuit Product Configuration - Saleable Product Id
description: Foreign key linking to the saleable product that can be produced by the processing circuit

Code identifying the specific operating configuration or mode used when producing this product from this circuit (e.g., CLEANER_ONLY, SCAV_RECYCLE, HIGH_GRADE_CAMPAIGN, BULK_PRODUCTION). Captures the operational setup that differentiates how different products are produced.

Product code of the primary output concentrate or processed product from this circuit (e.g., CU-CON-01 for copper concentrate). Links to sales contracts, logistics, and product quality specifications. [Moved from processing_circuit: This attribute in processing_circuit currently captures a single primary output product code. In a flexible processing operation where circuits can produce multiple products, this attribute should be removed from the circuit entity and the relationship should be captured through the circuit_product_configuration association. Each circuit-product configuration record will link to the saleable_product via FK, eliminating the need for a single product code on the circuit.]
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD; JORC Code; CIM Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of this circuit-product configuration. ACTIVE: currently in production use; PLANNED: approved for future implementation; SUSPENDED: temporarily inactive; DECOMMISSIONED: permanently retired; TESTING: under commissioning or trial.
Timestamp when this circuit-product configuration record was first created in the system.
Date on which this circuit-product configuration ceased or will cease to be active. Null indicates currently active configuration. Enables tracking of configuration lifecycle.
Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this circuit-product configuration record.

Integer ranking indicating the priority of this product within the circuit's production portfolio. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used for production scheduling and campaign planning when a circuit can produce multiple products.
Date from which this circuit-product configuration became or becomes active and operational. Enables tracking of configuration history and future planned configurations.

Target product grade for this specific circuit-product combination expressed as a percentage of valuable mineral content. This is configuration-specific as different products from the same circuit may have different grade targets (e.g., cleaner concentrate vs. rougher concentrate).

Target metallurgical recovery rate for this specific circuit-product combination expressed as a percentage. This is configuration-specific and may differ from the circuit's general design recovery rate depending on the product being produced and operating mode.
Unique surrogate identifier for this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration record

business_glossary_term: Circuit Tailings Routing - Processing Circuit Id
description: Foreign key linking to the processing circuit that generates the tailings stream
Identifier of the physical tailings pipeline infrastructure used for this circuit-to-TSF routing. Links routing configuration to physical asset register.
Foreign key linking to the Tailings Storage Facility receiving the tailings stream

Target slurry density for this specific circuit-to-TSF routing expressed as percentage solids by weight. May differ from circuit design density based on TSF deposition requirements and water recovery strategies.
Design basis dry solids flow rate from this circuit to this TSF expressed in tonnes per hour (tph). Used for TSF capacity planning and deposition rate modeling.
Target percentage of process water to be recovered from this tailings stream at the receiving TSF. Varies by TSF design (thickened tailings, paste, conventional) and water balance strategy.
Date from which this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration became or will become active. Supports time-based routing changes as TSFs reach capacity or new facilities are commissioned.
Date on which this circuit-to-TSF routing configuration ceased or will cease to be active. Null for currently active routings. Enables historical tracking of routing changes over mine life.

Business rule describing the geochemical criteria governing this routing decision (e.g., 'ARD-generating tailings from copper rougher circuit routed to lined TSF-3', 'Benign tailings from final cleaner routed to unlined TSF-1'). Critical for environmental compliance and acid rock drainage management.

Integer priority ranking for this routing configuration when multiple TSF destinations are available for a circuit (1=primary, 2=secondary, 3=tertiary). Drives automated routing logic and operational decision-making during TSF transitions.

Current operational status of this routing configuration. ACTIVE routings are currently in use, PLANNED are future configurations, INACTIVE are temporarily suspended, DECOMMISSIONED are permanently retired.

Code identifying the Tailings Storage Facility (TSF) or waste stream destination for tailings generated by this circuit. Critical for environmental compliance, TSF capacity planning, and regulatory reporting. [Moved from processing_circuit: This attribute in processing_circuit currently stores a single TSF destination code, implying a 1:N relationship. In the true M:N business reality where circuits can route to multiple TSFs based on operational conditions, this attribute should be removed and replaced by the circuit_tailings_routing association which captures the full many-to-many routing configuration with time-based and priority-based routing rules.]
reference: ISO 14001; ICMM Tailings Management; GRI 306; IsoMetrix

description: Classification of the tailings stream type for this routing (e.g., PRIMARY for main tailings flow, ARD for acid-generating tailings requiring lined storage, BENIGN for non-reactive tailings, EMERGENCY for overflow routing). Drives environmental compliance and TSF selection logic.

The unique laboratory assay reference number assigned by LabWare LIMS for the chemical analysis (assay) performed on this concentrate batch. Links the batch to its quality certificate and detailed elemental analysis results.

Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the concentrate batch, used across sales, logistics, and laboratory systems. Format: commodity prefix, year, and sequential number (e.g., CU-2024-000123). Sourced from LabWare LIMS batch numbering.

Current lifecycle status of the concentrate batch through the production-to-dispatch workflow: in_progress (being produced), sampled (sample taken for assay), assayed (lab results received), approved (quality approved for sale), dispatched (shipped to customer), rejected (failed quality control). Sourced from LabWare LIMS.
The primary commodity contained in this concentrate batch (e.g., copper, iron ore, lithium, nickel, coal). Drives downstream sales, logistics, and regulatory reporting classification.
reference: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards; ICMM

description: The grade of the primary commodity in the final concentrate product for this batch, expressed as a percentage (% Cu, % Fe, % Li, % Ni). The key product quality metric used in sales contracts and customer specifications. Sourced from LabWare LIMS assay results.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; ISO 11536 (Iron Ore Analysis)

description: Date and time when this concentrate batch record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and governance compliance.

The primary transport mode used to dispatch this concentrate batch from the processing plant to the port or customer (e.g., rail, road, ship, pipeline, conveyor). Determines logistics cost allocation and supply chain planning.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Supply Chain Management Standards

description: Dry weight of the concentrate batch in dry metric tonnes (DMT), calculated after moisture correction. The primary commercial weight measure used for sales contracts, invoicing, and production reporting. Key SSOT field for concentrate production output.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ISO 3087; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Electrical energy consumed per tonne of ore processed for this concentrate batch, expressed in kilowatt-hours per tonne (kWh/t). Sourced from OSIsoft PI System. Key OPEX and sustainability metric tracked against LOM plan targets.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 50001 (Energy Management); ICMM

description: Total dry metric tonnes of Run of Mine (ROM) ore fed into the processing circuit to produce this concentrate batch. Used as the denominator in recovery rate and yield calculations.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Caterpillar MineStar FMS

description: The grade of the primary commodity in the feed ore (Run of Mine (ROM)) entering the processing circuit for this batch, expressed as a percentage (%). Represents the input quality before beneficiation. Used for recovery rate calculation and reconciliation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; Geovia GEMS

description: Silica (SiO2) content in the concentrate batch expressed as a percentage (%). A key gangue impurity that affects product quality, smelter penalties, and customer acceptance. Sourced from LabWare LIMS assay results.
reference: LabWare LIMS; ISO 11536; Customer Product Specifications

description: Sulfur (S) content in the concentrate batch expressed as a percentage (%). A critical impurity for smelter operations and environmental compliance. High sulfur levels may attract penalties or rejection. Sourced from LabWare LIMS.
reference: LabWare LIMS; ISO 11536; Environmental Protection Regulations

description: Indicates whether this concentrate batch has passed quality control review and been formally approved for sale or dispatch. True = approved; False = pending or rejected. Set by the metallurgist or quality manager in LabWare LIMS.
Moisture content of the concentrate batch expressed as a percentage (%) of wet weight. Determined by laboratory analysis per ISO 3087. Critical for DMT calculation and product quality compliance.

The P80 particle size of the concentrate batch in micrometres (µm), representing the sieve size through which 80% of the material passes. Critical comminution (size reduction) quality parameter affecting downstream processing efficiency and product specification compliance.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; LabWare LIMS; ISO 4701 (Size Distribution)

description: The Incoterms trade term defining the price basis and risk transfer point for the sale of this concentrate batch (e.g., Free on Board (FOB), Cost Insurance and Freight (CIF)). Determines revenue recognition point and logistics cost allocation under IFRS 15.

The mineral processing route used to produce this concentrate batch (e.g., flotation, leaching, Dense Media Separation (DMS), Solvent Extraction Electrowinning (SX-EW), High Pressure Grinding Rolls (HPGR), Semi-Autogenous Grinding (SAG)). Determines applicable quality standards and reagent profiles. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flotation|leaching|DMS|SX-EW|HPGR|SAG|gravity|magnetic_separation — promote to reference product]
Calendar date on which this concentrate batch was produced at the processing plant. Used for daily production reporting and reconciliation against the production schedule.
Precise date and time when the concentrate batch production was completed and the batch was sealed/finalised at the processing plant. Sourced from OSIsoft PI System historian.

The provisional sale price per dry metric tonne (DMT) in US dollars (USD) agreed at the time of dispatch, subject to final price adjustment based on quotation period commodity prices. Used for initial revenue recognition under IFRS 15.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; IFRS 15; LME (London Metal Exchange)

description: Date and time when the concentrate batch was formally approved for sale following quality control review. Represents a key lifecycle milestone in the batch workflow. Sourced from LabWare LIMS.

The quality classification assigned to this concentrate batch based on assay results and product specification compliance. Grade A = premium specification met; Grade B = standard specification met; Grade C = marginal specification; off_spec = outside specification but saleable; rejected = failed quality control and cannot be sold.
reference: LabWare LIMS; Customer Product Specifications; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Total reagent consumption per tonne of ore processed for this concentrate batch, expressed in kilograms per tonne (kg/t). Aggregates all flotation, leaching, or other process reagents. Used for operating expenditure (OPEX) tracking and process efficiency analysis.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA CO; ICMM

description: The percentage of the valuable mineral in the feed ore that is successfully recovered into the concentrate product for this batch. Calculated as (concentrate grade × DMT) / (head grade × feed tonnes) × 100. Key processing efficiency KPI tracked against LOM plan targets.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ICMM Reporting Framework; OSIsoft PI System

description: The sales contract reference number under which this concentrate batch is sold to a customer. Links the production batch to the commercial sales agreement. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity of contract terms.
The date on which the representative sample was taken from this concentrate batch for laboratory assay analysis. Used for sample chain-of-custody tracking and quality control compliance.

The density of the concentrate slurry (water and ore mixture) in grams per cubic centimetre (g/cm³) at the point of batch finalisation. Monitored via OSIsoft PI System SCADA. Used for process control and dewatering circuit optimisation.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SCADA; Internal Process Standards

description: The average ore processing throughput rate in tonnes per hour (tph) achieved during the production of this concentrate batch. Sourced from OSIsoft PI System SCADA historian. Used for Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and capacity utilisation analysis.
Date and time when this concentrate batch record was last modified. Audit trail field used for change tracking, data lineage, and Silver Layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse.

Process water consumed per tonne of ore processed for this concentrate batch, expressed in cubic metres per tonne (m³/t). Critical environmental compliance metric reported under ISO 14001 and GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 14001; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

description: Total wet weight of the concentrate batch in metric tonnes (t) as measured at the processing plant prior to moisture correction. Used as the basis for moisture content calculation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ISO 3087 (Iron Ore Moisture Determination)

description: The mass yield of concentrate produced as a percentage of the total ore feed for this batch (DMT concentrate / feed tonnes × 100). Indicates the ratio of product output to ore input and is used for process efficiency benchmarking.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ICMM Reporting Framework

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each concentrate stockpile inventory record in the processing domain. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to sales.cargo_shipment. Business justification: Cargo shipments draw concentrate from stockpiles for vessel loading. Inventory reconciliation, demurrage management, and loading rate optimization require tracking which stockpile feeds each shipment.

Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Stockpiles hold specific commodities (iron ore concentrate, copper concentrate). Fundamental for inventory management, blending decisions, and production reconciliation. Replaces denormalized commodit

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Stockpile inventory is valued and tracked against cost centres for balance sheet reporting (IAS 2 inventory), NRV testing, and working capital management. Links physical inventory to financial asset a
Reference to the Life of Mine (LOM) plan against which this stockpile inventory is tracked for production target reconciliation.
Reference to the processing plant or facility that produced or holds this concentrate stockpile. Links to the plant master record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; OSIsoft PI System

description: Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Concentrate stockpiles track inventory against scheduled production for shipment planning, metal accounting, and working capital management. Critical for sales contract fulfillment and financial repor

Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Stockpiles contain specific saleable products awaiting dispatch. Essential for sales order fulfillment, inventory valuation, and linking physical inventory to sales contracts. Standard in mining logis

Foreign key linking to sales.shipment_nomination. Business justification: Shipment nominations allocate specific stockpile inventory to customer orders and vessel schedules. Logistics planning, inventory management, and customer delivery commitments depend on linking nomina

Foreign key linking to procurement.warehouse_location. Business justification: Concentrate stockpiles are physical storage locations requiring warehouse management for inventory reconciliation, site access control, environmental compliance, and security. Links processing output

Cumulative dry metric tonnes of concentrate added to this stockpile from production since the last inventory reconciliation period. Represents inflows from the processing circuit (e.g., flotation, leaching, SX-EW). Used in mass balance and inventory reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; OSIsoft PI System; ICMM Reporting

description: Target product grade (%) for this stockpile as specified in the blend optimisation plan or sales contract specification. Used to guide production blending decisions to meet customer or smelter feed requirements.
reference: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; Sales Contract Terms

description: Mineralogical classification of the concentrate product in this stockpile. Determines applicable processing routes, smelter penalty elements, and sales contract terms. E.g., sulphide concentrate from flotation vs oxide concentrate from leaching/SX-EW.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards

description: Timestamp when this concentrate stockpile record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record provenance and data lineage.

Indicates whether dust suppression measures (e.g., water sprays, chemical binders, covers) are currently applied to this stockpile. Relevant for environmental compliance, HSE reporting, and community impact management.
reference: IsoMetrix HSE; ISO 14001; MSHA Dust Control Standards

description: Chemical element or compound symbol for which the product_grade is reported (e.g., 'Cu' for copper, 'Fe' for iron, 'Li2O' for lithium oxide, 'Ni' for nickel). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the grade value across commodities.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards

description: Current physical inventory of concentrate in the stockpile expressed as dry metric tonnes (DMT), adjusted for moisture content. This is the primary inventory quantity used for sales nominations, shipping calculations, and inventory reconciliation. Updated after each survey event.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; ICMM Reporting; FOB/CIF contract terms

description: Current physical inventory of concentrate in the stockpile expressed as wet metric tonnes (WMT), inclusive of moisture. Used for physical handling, transport weight calculations, and logistics planning. Distinct from DMT which is the commercial quantity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Pronto Xi Inventory

description: Indicates whether this stockpile inventory has been nominated against an active shipment or vessel loading schedule. True = nominated for an upcoming shipment; False = available for future nomination. Supports logistics scheduling and sales operations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD; Pronto Xi; FOB/CIF Contract Terms

description: Indicates whether this stockpile is subject to an environmental hold that restricts movement or shipment of material (e.g., pending EIS review, acid rock drainage concern, or regulatory compliance investigation). True = hold in place; False = no environmental restriction.
reference: IsoMetrix HSE; ISO 14001; EIS Regulatory Requirements

description: Date of the most recent laboratory assay used to determine the current product grade and moisture content of the stockpile. Used to assess grade data currency for sales nominations and blend optimisation.

Date of the most recent physical survey or measurement used to determine the current stockpile inventory volume and tonnage. Critical for assessing inventory data currency and triggering re-survey workflows when data is stale.
reference: Internal Survey SOP; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Target concentrate inventory level in dry metric tonnes as specified in the Life of Mine (LOM) plan for the current period. Used to assess inventory performance against plan and trigger production rate adjustments.

Engineered maximum storage capacity of the stockpile expressed in dry metric tonnes (DMT). Used for capacity planning, logistics scheduling, and triggering production rate adjustments when inventory approaches capacity limits.
reference: Mine Planning SOP; SAP S/4HANA MM; Hexagon MinePlan

description: Maximum allowable moisture content (%) for this stockpile as defined by the applicable sales contract, shipping specification, or transportable moisture limit (TML) under the IMSBC Code. Exceedance triggers quarantine or drying operations.
reference: IMSBC Code (IMO); Sales Contract Terms; ISO 3087

description: Minimum acceptable product grade (%) for this stockpile as defined by the applicable sales contract or offtake agreement. Material below this threshold may be subject to penalty pricing or rejection.

Unique surrogate identifier for this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration. Primary key for the tailings routing association.

Business identifier for the physical tailings pipeline that connects this processing plant to this TSF. Multiple plants may share pipeline infrastructure or a single plant may have dedicated pipelines to different TSFs. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because it represents the physical connection infrastructure specific to this plant-TSF pair.
Foreign key linking to the source processing plant that generates the tailings stream
Foreign key linking to the destination Tailings Storage Facility that receives the tailings stream

Date when this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration was commissioned and became operational. This is distinct from the plant commissioning date or TSF commissioning date because routing connections are established independently as infrastructure is built or modified. Critical for tracking operational history and regulatory compliance.

Date when this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration was decommissioned and ceased operation. Null if the routing is still active. Routing may be decommissioned when TSFs reach capacity, pipelines are retired, or plant operations are reconfigured, even if both the plant and TSF remain operational with other routing configurations.

Design volumetric flow rate of tailings slurry through this routing configuration, expressed in cubic meters per hour (m³/h). This is specific to the routing because it depends on pipeline diameter, pump capacity, elevation change, and distance between the specific plant and TSF. Critical for hydraulic design and operational planning.

Design solids content of the tailings slurry for this specific plant-to-TSF routing, expressed as percentage by weight (0-100). This varies by routing because different TSFs may require different slurry densities based on dam design, deposition method, and storage capacity constraints. Critical for pipeline design, pumping requirements, and TSF water balance.

Net elevation gain (or loss if negative) from the processing plant discharge point to the TSF deposition point for this specific routing, measured in meters. This is a relationship attribute because it describes the topographic profile of this specific plant-TSF connection. Critical for pump sizing and energy consumption calculations.

Boolean flag indicating whether this TSF is the primary (normal operating) destination for tailings from this processing plant. True = primary destination; False = secondary/emergency destination. A plant typically has one primary TSF and may have one or more secondary TSFs for contingency operations, maintenance periods, or capacity management. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because it describes the operational priority of this specific plant-TSF connection.

Current operational state of this specific plant-to-TSF routing configuration. Active = currently in use; Standby = commissioned but not currently routing tailings (emergency backup); Decommissioned = permanently retired; Under-construction = pipeline and infrastructure being built. This status is independent of the plant and TSF operational statuses because routing configurations can be in standby while both endpoints are active.

Total length of the tailings pipeline for this specific plant-to-TSF routing, measured in kilometers. This is a relationship attribute because it describes the physical connection infrastructure between this specific plant-TSF pair. Relevant for pumping energy calculations, maintenance planning, and risk assessment.

Classification of the tailings stream type being routed from this plant to this TSF. Conventional tailings are slurry with 20-30% solids; thickened tailings are 45-55% solids; paste tailings are 65-75% solids; filtered tailings are dewatered to 80%+ solids; co-disposal includes waste rock. This attribute belongs to the routing relationship because the same plant may produce different stream types for different TSFs depending on processing method and TSF design requirements.
