description: Specific gravity (SG) of the dense medium (typically ferrosilicon or magnetite suspension) used in the DMS circuit during this event. The primary separation control parameter — particles denser than the medium sink, lighter particles float.
reference: OSIsoft PI System — SCADA Integration; Internal DMS Operating Standard

description: Mass of dense medium (ferrosilicon or magnetite) lost per tonne of feed processed during this DMS event, measured in kg/t. Medium losses are a significant operating cost driver and are tracked for reagent consumption reporting and OPEX management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO — Cost Management; Internal OPEX Reporting Standard

description: Ratio of dense medium volume to ore feed volume in the DMS circuit during this event. A key process control parameter affecting separation efficiency and medium stability. Typically expressed as m³ medium per tonne of ore.
reference: OSIsoft PI System — Process Data Historian; Internal DMS SOP

description: Type of dense medium used in the DMS circuit. Ferrosilicon is used for higher-density separations (diamonds, iron ore), while magnetite is common for coal DMS circuits. Affects reagent cost and medium recovery efficiency.

Geological classification of the ore feed processed during this DMS event (e.g., oxide, sulphide, transitional, ROM blend). Influences medium density settings and expected sink/float yields. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oxide|sulphide|transitional|rom_blend|high_ash|low_ash|coking|thermal — promote to reference product]
reference: JORC Code 2012 — Ore Type Classification; Geovia GEMS

description: Grade of the valuable mineral in the DMS product stream, expressed as a percentage. For coal, this is ash content of clean coal; for iron ore, this is Fe%; for diamonds, this is carats per hundred tonnes (cpht). Benchmarked against LOM plan targets.
reference: JORC Code 2012 — Grade Reporting; LabWare LIMS — Assay Results

description: Calendar date on which this DMS event occurred, used for daily production reporting, metallurgical balance reconciliation, and LOM plan variance tracking.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Internal Production Reporting Standard

description: Planned metallurgical recovery rate target for the DMS circuit during this event period, sourced from the LOM plan or shift production plan. Enables real-time variance tracking against actual circuit_recovery_pct.
reference: Deswik — Mine Scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: Grade of the valuable mineral in the DMS reject (discard) stream, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess mineral losses to tailings and validate separation efficiency. High reject grade indicates potential recovery improvement opportunity.
reference: JORC Code 2012 — Grade Reporting; LabWare LIMS — Assay Results

description: Classification of the shift period during which the DMS event occurred (day, afternoon, or night). Used for shift-comparative performance analysis and crew scheduling.
Total dry metric tonnes (DMT) of material reporting to the sink stream during this DMS event. Used for mass balance closure, metallurgical accounting, and product inventory reconciliation.
reference: JORC Code 2012 — Mass Balance; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

description: Percentage of the DMS feed that reports to the sink (dense) product stream, expressed as a mass percentage. For coal DMS, the sink is typically the reject (high-ash discard); for iron ore and diamonds, the sink is the valuable product.
reference: JORC Code 2012 — Yield Reporting; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

description: Originating operational system from which this DMS event record was sourced. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and data quality assessment in the silver layer lakehouse. Typically OSIsoft PI System via SCADA integration or manual entry.
reference: Internal Data Governance and Lineage Standard; Databricks Lakehouse Architecture

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this DMS event record, supporting audit trail and data quality monitoring.
Unique surrogate identifier for each ore feed stream record entering the processing plant. Primary key for the feed_stream data product.

Reference identifier for the primary conveyor or feeder equipment delivering material to this feed stream. Links to the equipment asset register for maintenance scheduling and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) tracking.
reference: Infor EAM; Caterpillar MineStar; SAP S/4HANA PM

description: Reference identifier for the specific processing circuit (e.g., SAG/Ball Mill circuit, DMS circuit, flotation circuit) that this feed stream feeds into. Enables circuit-level mass balance and throughput analysis.

Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Feed streams carry specific commodities from mine to plant. Fundamental for grade control, blending decisions, and feed scheduling. Replaces denormalized commodity text field with proper FK for refere

Reference identifier for the LOM (Life of Mine) plan version that defines the target feed parameters for this stream. Enables variance analysis between planned and actual feed characteristics for production reconciliation.

Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Feed streams originate from specific orebodies. Mine-to-mill optimization and metallurgical reconciliation require tracking which orebody supplies each feed stream to correlate geological characterist
Reference identifier for the mineral processing plant or facility that this feed stream supplies. Supports multi-plant operations and mass balance reporting at plant level.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM; OSIsoft PI System

description: Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Feed streams must reference production schedules to track which mine production periods feed which processing campaigns. Essential for ore type scheduling, blend optimization, and integrated mine-mill

Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Feed streams originate from specific prospects/orebodies. Critical for mine-to-mill optimization, ore tracking, metallurgical reconciliation, and LOM planning. Real business need: tracking ore source
Reference identifier for the specific physical source location (ROM pad, stockpile, crusher station) from which this feed stream originates. Links to the plant location or stockpile master.

Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Feed streams originate from ore extracted from specific tenements. Essential for royalty calculations, grade reconciliation against tenement reserves, and compliance with tenement-specific production

Bond Abrasion Index (Ai) of the ore in the feed stream, a dimensionless measure of ore abrasiveness. Drives liner and media wear rate predictions for SAG mills, ball mills, and HPGR (High Pressure Grinding Rolls), informing maintenance scheduling and OPEX forecasting.
reference: LabWare LIMS; Infor EAM; JORC Code 2012

description: Bond Ball Mill Work Index (BWi) of the ore expressed in kilowatt-hours per tonne (kWh/t). Measures ore hardness and grindability; used to predict mill power requirements, throughput, and energy consumption in comminution circuit design and optimisation.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Bulk density of the ore material in the feed stream expressed in tonnes per cubic metre (t/m³). Used to convert volumetric flow measurements to mass flow for mass balance calculations and stockpile volume reconciliation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; Geovia GEMS

description: The date on which this feed stream was formally commissioned and accepted into operational service. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, warranty management, and CAPEX (Capital Expenditure) project closure reporting.
reference: Infor EAM; SAP S/4HANA PS; ISO 14001

description: The timestamp when this feed stream record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data lineage and record provenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: ISO 14001; IFRS 6; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

description: The minimum economic grade threshold (cut-off grade) applied to material entering this feed stream. Material below cut-off grade is classified as waste and diverted to the waste dump. Defined per LOM plan and commodity economics.

Maximum rated throughput capacity of the feed stream infrastructure (conveyor, feeder, chute) in dry metric tonnes per hour. Used for bottleneck analysis and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculations.

Percentage of waste material mixed with ore in the feed stream due to mining dilution. Dilution reduces the effective head grade and is tracked for reconciliation between geological resource model grades and actual plant feed grades.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS

description: The date from which this feed stream definition and its associated parameters (nominal rate, target grade, processing route) became operationally effective. Supports temporal versioning of feed stream configurations aligned to LOM plan revisions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: The date on which this feed stream definition ceases to be operationally effective. Null indicates the stream is currently active with no planned end date. Supports LOM plan stage transitions and plant reconfiguration tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: Temperature of the ore or slurry in the feed stream measured in degrees Celsius. Relevant for leaching circuits (SX-EW), autoclave operations, and cold-climate operations where freezing affects conveyor and crusher performance.

Percentage of waste rock (gangue) minerals in the feed stream material. High gangue content increases dilution, reduces effective head grade, and impacts reagent consumption in flotation and leaching circuits.

The assay-determined grade of the primary valuable mineral in the feed stream expressed as a percentage (e.g., % Fe for iron ore, % Cu for copper). Head grade is the key input for recovery rate calculations and production reconciliation against the LOM plan.
reference: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; Geovia GEMS

description: Moisture content of the ore in the feed stream expressed as a percentage of total wet mass. Moisture affects conveyor performance, crusher throughput, mill power draw, and dry tonne calculations for mass balance and invoicing.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; ISO 3087 (Coal Moisture)

description: The design or nameplate feed rate for this stream expressed in dry metric tonnes per hour (tph). Represents the target throughput capacity used in LOM (Life of Mine) plan scheduling and plant design. Distinct from actual measured feed rate.

Geological ore type classification of the material in this feed stream (e.g., oxide, sulphide, transitional, fresh, weathered). Ore type drives processing route selection, reagent dosing, and expected recovery rates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oxide|sulphide|transitional|fresh|weathered|mixed|high_grade|low_grade — promote to reference product]
reference: JORC Code 2012; Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan

description: The 50th percentile (median) passing particle size of the feed stream material in millimetres. Complements P80 to characterise the full particle size distribution (PSD) shape, supporting comminution circuit modelling and screen efficiency analysis.

The 80th percentile passing particle size of the feed stream material expressed in millimetres (mm). P80 is the industry-standard metric for characterising particle size distribution (PSD) in comminution circuits. Critical input for SAG mill and HPGR (High Pressure Grinding Rolls) performance modelling.
reference: JORC Code 2012; OSIsoft PI System; LabWare LIMS

description: The OSIsoft PI System historian tag name for the real-time feed rate measurement instrument (belt scale or flow meter) associated with this feed stream. Enables direct linkage between the data product and the SCADA/PI process historian for real-time and historical data retrieval.

business_glossary_term: OSIsoft PI Tag - Particle Size Analyser
description: The OSIsoft PI System historian tag name for the online particle size analyser (PSA) instrument monitoring P80 for this feed stream. Supports real-time comminution circuit control and automated variance alerting.

The designated mineral processing route for material in this feed stream (e.g., SAG/Ball Mill comminution, DMS (Dense Media Separation), flotation, leaching, SX-EW (Solvent Extraction Electrowinning)). Determines downstream circuit routing and reagent requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sag_ball_mill|hpgr|dms|flotation|leaching|sx_ew|gravity|magnetic_separation|cil|cip — promote to reference product]
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Hexagon MinePlan; JORC Code 2012

description: Density of the ore-water slurry mixture in the feed stream expressed in tonnes per cubic metre. Applicable to wet processing circuits (SAG mill discharge, flotation feed). Monitored via OSIsoft PI System for real-time process control.

Percentage of solids by mass in the slurry feed stream (percent solids). A key process control parameter for wet grinding and flotation circuits; directly affects mill power draw, pump performance, and flotation cell residence time.

Classification of the physical origin point from which ore material enters this feed stream. ROM (Run of Mine) pad indicates direct truck tip; stockpile indicates reclaimed material; crusher indicates post-comminution feed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rom_pad|primary_crusher|secondary_crusher|tertiary_crusher|stockpile|reclaim_conveyor|direct_tip|sag_discharge — promote to reference product]

Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the feed stream within the processing plant configuration (e.g., FS-ROM-001, FS-CRU-002). Used in mass balance reconciliation and plant P&ID references.
Descriptive human-readable name of the feed stream (e.g., 'Primary ROM Feed', 'SAG Mill Discharge', 'Crusher Product Recirculating Load'). Used in operational dashboards and reporting.

Current lifecycle status of the feed stream definition within the processing plant. Active streams are currently receiving material; suspended streams are temporarily offline; decommissioned streams are permanently retired from the circuit.

Classification of the feed stream by its position and role in the comminution circuit. ROM (Run of Mine) feed is direct from the ROM pad; crushed feed is post-primary crusher; recirculating load is material returned for regrinding. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rom_feed|crushed_feed|recirculating_load|classifier_overflow|classifier_underflow|screen_oversize|sag_discharge|ball_mill_discharge — promote to reference product]

The planned or scheduled feed rate for this stream in dry metric tonnes per hour as defined in the current production schedule or LOM plan. Distinct from nominal (design) feed rate; used for shift-level production planning and variance reporting.
reference: Deswik; Hexagon MinePlan; SAP S/4HANA PS

description: The planned head grade of the primary valuable mineral for this feed stream as per the current production schedule or LOM plan. Used for production reconciliation and variance analysis against actual assayed head grade.

The planned P80 particle size target for this feed stream in millimetres as specified in the processing plant design or LOM plan. Used to assess crusher and mill performance against design specifications.
reference: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; OSIsoft PI System

description: Maximum lump size of material in the feed stream expressed in millimetres. Defines the upper bound of the particle size distribution and is critical for crusher gap settings, conveyor design, and mill liner protection.
The timestamp when this feed stream record was most recently modified. Supports incremental data loading, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail requirements in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: ISO 14001; IFRS 6; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each flotation circuit performance record per shift. Primary key for this transactional entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA CO

description: Reference to the flotation circuit (e.g., rougher, scavenger, cleaner bank) where this event was recorded. Links to the processing circuit master resource. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE / resource reference category.

Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Flotation circuits target specific minerals/commodities (copper, nickel, zinc). Core to recovery tracking, circuit optimization, and metallurgical reporting. Domain experts expect commodity-specific f

Reference to the metallurgist responsible for reviewing and approving this flotation event record. Ensures accountability in metallurgical accounting sign-off and supports regulatory reporting requirements. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: Foreign key linking to processing.feed_stream. Business justification: Flotation events process specific feed streams. One event processes one feed stream; one feed stream has many events. This links the flotation event to the feed stream being processed.

Foreign key linking to hse.incident. Business justification: Flotation involves chemical reagents (collectors, frothers, depressants) and mechanical hazards (impellers, agitators). Incidents during flotation operations (chemical spills, equipment failures, expo

Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory. Business justification: Flotation circuit samples (feed, concentrate, tailings) are sent to designated labs for grade and recovery verification. Critical for process control, circuit optimization, and validating online analy

Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Flotation cell mechanical issues (impeller wear, air system failures) during events trigger maintenance work orders. Links flotation performance problems to maintenance interventions for recovery opti
Reference to the mineral processing plant or concentrator facility where the flotation circuit operates. Enables plant-level aggregation and benchmarking across sites.

Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Flotation events track recovery performance against scheduled mine production for metallurgical accounting, ore type performance analysis, and integrated mine-mill optimization. Essential for recovery

Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Flotation performance varies by ore source/prospect. Critical for metallurgical testwork validation, circuit optimization, and ore blending strategies. Real business need: ore-specific recovery tracki

Foreign key linking to processing.shift_production_run. Business justification: Flotation events occur during a production shift run. One flotation event belongs to one shift run; one shift run has many flotation events. This links the event to the processing domain's shift entit
Reference to the operational shift during which this flotation event was recorded. Enables shift-level metallurgical accounting and performance comparison across day, afternoon, and night shifts.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; OSIsoft PI System

description: Foreign key linking to tailings.tsf. Business justification: Flotation circuits generate tailings streams deposited to specific TSF. Critical for metallurgical balance closure, TSF capacity management, and geochemical characterization. Tracks tailings_mass_t de

business_glossary_term: Air Flow Rate (Cubic Metres Per Minute)
description: Volumetric flow rate of air injected into the flotation cells, measured in cubic metres per minute (m³/min). Air flow is a primary control variable affecting bubble generation, froth stability, and mineral recovery. Monitored via OSIsoft PI SCADA integration.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Number of flotation cells actively operating in the circuit during this event period. Cells may be taken offline for maintenance or cleaning. Operating cell count affects residence time and overall circuit capacity. Sourced from Infor EAM work order data.

Total active volume of the flotation cells in operation during this event, measured in cubic metres (m³). Combined with feed rate, determines slurry residence time which is a key flotation kinetics parameter.
reference: Infor EAM; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Percentage of the event period during which the flotation circuit was available and operating (not in planned or unplanned downtime). Calculated as operating hours divided by scheduled hours × 100. Contributes to Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) reporting.
reference: Infor EAM; OSIsoft PI System; ICMM OEE Guidelines

description: Percentage of the valuable mineral in the feed that is recovered into the concentrate product for this flotation circuit stage. Calculated as: (concentrate mass × concentrate grade) / (feed mass × feed grade) × 100. Core metallurgical KPI for LOM plan tracking and reagent optimisation. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category.
reference: ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: The specific stage of the flotation circuit captured in this event record. Rougher is the primary separation stage; scavenger recovers minerals from rougher tailings; cleaner upgrades rougher concentrate grade; recleaner further upgrades cleaner concentrate. Critical for stage-by-stage metallurgical accounting.
reference: ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Dosage rate of the collector reagent (e.g., xanthate, dithiophosphate) added to the flotation circuit, expressed in grams per dry metric tonne of feed (g/t). Collector promotes hydrophobicity of target mineral surfaces to enable bubble attachment. Key reagent optimisation variable.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Pronto Xi Inventory; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Grade of the valuable mineral in the flotation concentrate product, expressed as a percentage (%). Measures the quality of the separation achieved. Higher concentrate grade reduces downstream smelting costs and improves payable metal. Sourced from LabWare LIMS.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: The planned or contractually required concentrate grade for the valuable mineral, expressed as a percentage (%). Used to assess whether the flotation circuit is meeting product quality specifications for offtake agreements and smelter contracts.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD; Hexagon MinePlan; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: Total dry mass of concentrate produced by the flotation circuit during the event period, measured in dry metric tonnes (t). Used in metallurgical accounting mass balance and payable metal calculations.
reference: ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA

description: Timestamp when this flotation event record was first captured in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.

Dosage rate of the depressant reagent (e.g., sodium cyanide, zinc sulphate, CMC) added to the flotation circuit, expressed in grams per dry metric tonne of feed (g/t). Depressants selectively prevent flotation of gangue minerals or penalty elements, improving concentrate grade and selectivity.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Pronto Xi Inventory; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Descriptive reason for any unplanned or planned downtime experienced by the flotation circuit during this event period (e.g., pump failure, cell maintenance, reagent outage, power interruption). Null if no downtime occurred. Used for reliability analysis and maintenance planning in Infor EAM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pump_failure|cell_maintenance|reagent_outage|power_interruption|planned_shutdown|instrumentation_fault — promote to reference product]

The real-world timestamp marking the end of the flotation measurement period (typically shift end). Combined with start timestamp to define the measurement window for throughput and reagent consumption calculations.

Externally-known business identifier for this flotation event record, formatted as FLT-YYYY-MM-DD-NNNN. Used for cross-system reference, metallurgical accounting reconciliation, and audit trail. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA

description: The real-world timestamp marking the start of the flotation measurement period (typically shift start). Used for time-series alignment with OSIsoft PI historian data and SCADA records. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.

Current workflow state of the flotation event record. Draft indicates data entry in progress; confirmed indicates shift data locked; reviewed indicates metallurgist sign-off; approved indicates inclusion in metallurgical balance; voided indicates record invalidated. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: Head grade of the valuable mineral (e.g., copper, lithium, nickel) in the flotation feed, expressed as a percentage (%). Derived from assay results and used as the denominator in circuit recovery calculations. Sourced from LabWare LIMS assay data.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: The 80th percentile passing particle size (P80) of the flotation feed, measured in micrometres (µm). Particle size is a critical determinant of flotation performance — coarse particles are difficult to float while ultra-fine particles suffer from poor bubble attachment. Sourced from LabWare LIMS particle size analysis.
reference: LabWare LIMS; SME Mineral Processing Handbook; JORC Code 2012

description: Mass flow rate of ore slurry fed into the flotation circuit during the event period, measured in dry metric tonnes per hour (t/h). Key throughput metric for metallurgical accounting and LOM plan performance tracking.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: Depth of the froth layer maintained in the flotation cell during the event period, measured in millimetres (mm). Froth depth is a critical control parameter influencing concentrate grade and recovery trade-off. Deeper froth generally improves grade at the expense of recovery.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Dosage rate of the frother reagent (e.g., MIBC, pine oil, polyglycol) added to the flotation circuit, expressed in grams per dry metric tonne of feed (g/t). Frother stabilises the froth layer and controls bubble size distribution. Critical for froth stability and concentrate transport.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Pronto Xi Inventory; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Average rotational speed of the flotation cell impellers during the event period, measured in revolutions per minute (RPM). Impeller speed controls slurry agitation, air dispersion, and bubble-particle contact. Monitored via OSIsoft PI SCADA.

Dosage rate of lime (calcium hydroxide or calcium oxide) added to the flotation circuit for pH control, expressed in kilograms per dry metric tonne of feed (kg/t). Lime is typically the highest-volume reagent in sulphide flotation circuits and a significant OPEX driver.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Pronto Xi Inventory; SAP S/4HANA CO

description: The ratio of concentrate mass to feed mass expressed as a percentage (%). Indicates the proportion of total feed mass reporting to the concentrate. High mass pull may indicate over-flotation and gangue entrainment; low mass pull may indicate under-recovery. Key flotation control parameter.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: The primary valuable mineral being recovered in this flotation circuit event (e.g., copper, nickel, lithium). Determines the applicable reagent suite, recovery benchmarks, and product specifications. Essential for multi-commodity processing plants. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: copper|nickel|lithium|zinc|lead|molybdenum|gold|silver — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: JORC Code 2012; LabWare LIMS; Geovia GEMS

description: Classification of the ore type being processed in the flotation circuit during this event (e.g., sulphide, oxide, mixed, transitional). Ore type significantly influences reagent selection, dosage rates, and achievable recovery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sulphide|oxide|mixed|transitional|primary|secondary — promote to reference product]

Solids content of the flotation feed slurry expressed as a percentage by mass (% solids). Pulp density affects reagent effectiveness, bubble-particle collision rates, and overall flotation kinetics. Monitored continuously via OSIsoft PI.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: pH of the flotation pulp during the event period. pH is a critical chemical environment parameter that governs mineral surface chemistry, collector adsorption, and selectivity between valuable minerals and gangue. Typically controlled with lime addition.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: The planned or budgeted circuit recovery percentage for this flotation stage as defined in the LOM plan or metallurgical design criteria. Enables variance analysis between actual and target recovery for performance management and LOM plan tracking.
reference: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; JORC Code 2012; ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines

description: The LabWare LIMS sample identifier for the assay samples collected during this flotation event (feed, concentrate, and tailings). Enables traceability between the flotation performance record and the underlying laboratory assay results supporting grade data.

Temperature of the flotation feed slurry during the event period, measured in degrees Celsius (°C). Slurry temperature affects reagent solubility, reaction kinetics, and froth stability. Particularly relevant in cold-climate operations and heated leach-flotation circuits.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SME Mineral Processing Handbook

description: Grade of the valuable mineral remaining in the flotation tailings stream, expressed as a percentage (%). Indicates mineral losses to the Tailings Storage Facility (TSF). Used to calculate circuit recovery and identify optimisation opportunities. Sourced from LabWare LIMS.
reference: LabWare LIMS; JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Total dry mass of tailings discharged from the flotation circuit during the event period, measured in dry metric tonnes (t). Used in mass balance reconciliation and TSF volumetric planning.
reference: ICMM Metallurgical Accounting Guidelines; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Timestamp when this flotation event record was last modified. Tracks data corrections, metallurgist adjustments, and re-assay updates. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.

business_glossary_term: Water Addition Rate (Cubic Metres Per Hour)
description: Rate of process water added to the flotation circuit to maintain target pulp density, measured in cubic metres per hour (m³/h). Water consumption is a key environmental and OPEX metric, particularly in water-stressed mining regions subject to ISO 14001 reporting.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 14001 Environmental Management; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

reference: SAP S/4HANA HR/PP Module; Mine Shift Schedule

description: Nameplate design throughput capacity of the plant expressed in dry metric tonnes per hour (tph) of Run of Mine (ROM) feed. Represents the engineering-rated maximum throughput under optimal conditions. Used as the denominator for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculations.
reference: JORC Code 2012; ICMM Technical Guidelines; Infor EAM

description: Elevation of the processing plant site in metres above sea level (mASL). Relevant for water balance modelling, slurry pipeline hydraulics design, and environmental impact assessments.

Design ROM feed head grade (percentage of valuable mineral in the feed ore) for which the plant was engineered. Used as the baseline for metallurgical balance calculations, cut-off grade assessments, and LOM plan modelling.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; Geovia GEMS; Hexagon MinePlan

description: Geographic latitude of the processing plant centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS (Geographic Information System) mapping, spatial analysis, and environmental impact zone delineation.

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Plant Code
description: The plant identifier used in the LabWare LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System) for sample registration, assay result linkage, and metallurgical accounting. Enables traceability from plant feed to product assay.
Geographic longitude of the processing plant centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and environmental impact zone delineation.

Design-rated metallurgical recovery rate expressed as a percentage (0–100). Represents the percentage of the target valuable mineral in the feed that is expected to report to the concentrate or product stream under nameplate conditions. Key input to LOM plan financial modelling and JORC/NI 43-101 resource estimation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC; CIM Standards

description: Total count of parallel processing lines (circuits) within the plant. Each line represents an independent processing train capable of treating ore from feed to product. Drives capacity planning, maintenance scheduling, and redundancy analysis.

Current lifecycle state of the processing plant. 'active' = fully operational; 'care-and-maintenance' = temporarily idle but preserved; 'decommissioned' = permanently closed; 'commissioning' = in start-up phase; 'suspended' = temporarily halted due to regulatory or operational reasons.
reference: ICMM Mine Closure Framework; ISO 14001; Infor EAM

description: Comma-separated list of ore/commodity types this plant is designed and certified to process (e.g., 'iron ore, copper, gold, lithium, nickel, coal, diamonds'). Drives feed stream routing and LOM plan alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iron ore|copper|gold|lithium|nickel|coal|diamonds|zinc|lead|manganese — promote to reference product]

Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the processing plant, used across ERP, SCADA, and FMS systems (e.g., 'PP-PILBARA-01', 'PROC-CU-02'). Unique across the enterprise and referenced in operational reporting.

Free-text narrative description of the processing plant including key design features, processing circuit configuration, historical context, and any notable operational characteristics. Supports regulatory submissions, investor reports, and technical documentation.
reference: JORC Code 2012; SEC S-K 1300; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

description: Full human-readable name of the mineral processing plant facility (e.g., 'Pilbara Iron Ore Processing Plant 1', 'Olympic Dam Copper Concentrator'). Used in reports, dashboards, and regulatory submissions.

High-level classification of the processing plant by metallurgical process family. 'concentrator' = physical separation to produce mineral concentrate; 'hydrometallurgical' = chemical leaching/SX-EW; 'pyrometallurgical' = smelting/roasting; 'beneficiation' = upgrading without full extraction; 'refinery' = final product refining; 'pelletising' = iron ore pellet production.

Nameplate design electrical power consumption in kilowatts (kW) at full throughput. Used for energy cost modelling (OPEX), carbon footprint reporting (GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement), and grid capacity planning.
reference: GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement; ISO 14001; ICMM

description: The principal mineral processing and beneficiation method employed by this plant. Comminution includes SAG/HPGR milling; flotation covers froth flotation separation; leaching includes heap and tank leaching; SX-EW (Solvent Extraction Electrowinning) for copper cathode production; DMS (Dense Media Separation) for coal/diamonds; gravity and magnetic separation for iron ore. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: comminution|flotation|leaching|SX-EW|DMS|gravity|magnetic — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

The primary saleable product form produced by this plant (e.g., 'concentrate' for copper/gold flotation plants, 'cathode' for SX-EW copper plants, 'pellet' for iron ore pelletising, 'fines'/'lump' for iron ore beneficiation, 'doré' for gold/silver). Drives sales contract and logistics configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: concentrate|cathode|pellet|fines|lump|slurry|doré — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The timestamp when this processing plant master record was first created in the data platform (Silver Layer). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and regulatory record-keeping obligations.
The timestamp when this processing plant master record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit compliance.

The SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance (PM) functional location code assigned to this processing plant. Enables linkage to maintenance work orders, preventive maintenance plans, and CAPEX/OPEX cost centre reporting in SAP.

The identifier of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system instance or node that monitors and controls this processing plant. Used to link real-time process historian data (OSIsoft PI System) to the plant master record.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SCADA Integration Standards

description: State, province, or territory in which the processing plant is located (e.g., 'Western Australia', 'British Columbia', 'Antofagasta'). Used for jurisdictional regulatory compliance, environmental permitting, and geographic reporting.

business_glossary_term: Design Tailings Generation Rate (Tonnes Per Hour)
description: Nameplate design rate of tailings (gangue and process residue) generated by the plant in dry metric tonnes per hour. Drives TSF (Tailings Storage Facility) capacity planning, environmental licence conditions, and ICMM tailings governance compliance.
reference: ICMM Tailings Governance Standard; ISO 14001; EIS

description: Design target grade of the primary valuable mineral in the final product expressed as a percentage (e.g., 28.5% Cu in copper concentrate, 62% Fe in iron ore lump). Used as the benchmark for metallurgical performance assessment and sales contract compliance.
reference: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC; LabWare LIMS

business_glossary_term: Design Water Consumption (Cubic Metres Per Hour)
description: Nameplate design water consumption rate in cubic metres per hour (m³/h) for the plant under full throughput conditions. Critical for water balance management, environmental licence compliance, and EIS (Environmental Impact Statement) reporting.
reference: ISO 14001; EIS Regulatory Requirements; ICMM Water Stewardship

description: Primary key for plant_utility_consumption
Identifier of the employee (typically the plant metallurgist or environmental officer) who approved this utility consumption record for OPEX posting and regulatory reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001

description: Identifier of the specific processing circuit (e.g., SAG mill, flotation, leaching, SX-EW) for which utility consumption is recorded. Enables circuit-level OPEX benchmarking.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Asset Framework; Internal Circuit Register

description: Reference to the Life of Mine (LOM) plan version against which utility consumption targets and budgets are benchmarked. Supports variance analysis against LOM plan targets.
reference: Deswik LOM Planning; Internal LOM Plan Register

description: Identifier of the mineral processing plant where utility consumption was recorded. Links to the plant master record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM Functional Location; Internal Plant Master

description: Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Utility consumption must be tracked against production schedules for cost allocation, energy intensity benchmarking, and carbon accounting. Essential for AISC calculation and Scope 1/2 emissions repor

Foreign key linking to processing.shift_production_run. Business justification: Utility consumption is recorded per shift run. One consumption record belongs to one shift run; one shift run has many consumption records. This links the utility consumption to the processing domain'
Identifier of the production shift during which this utility consumption was recorded. Links to the shift production run record for operational context.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP-PI; Internal Shift Schedule

description: Date and time when the utility consumption record was approved by the authorised employee. Marks the record as locked for OPEX cost posting and environmental compliance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO; Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001

description: Approved carbon budget allocation for this circuit and period in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent (tCO₂e), derived from the LOM plan carbon budget. Used to calculate emissions variance and compliance status.
reference: ICMM Climate Change Position Statement; NGER Act; Internal LOM Plan Carbon Budget

description: Volume of compressed air consumed by the circuit during the period in standard cubic metres (Sm³). Used for flotation cell aeration, instrumentation, and pneumatic equipment. Contributes to energy OPEX.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Internal OPEX Reporting Standard

description: Externally-known business reference number for this utility consumption record, used for cross-referencing with SAP S/4HANA CO cost postings and OPEX reporting. Format: UC-YYYY-MM-NNNNNN.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; Internal OPEX Reporting Standard

description: Date and time when this utility consumption record was first created in the system, sourced from OSIsoft PI System historian ingestion or manual entry. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001 Audit Trail

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary cost fields in this record (e.g., AUD, USD, ZAR). Ensures consistent currency context for OPEX reporting and financial consolidation.
reference: ISO 4217; IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Currency Configuration

description: Origin system or method by which utility consumption data was captured. PI System and SCADA sources are automated and high-confidence; manual_entry and estimated records require additional validation before use in regulatory reporting.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SCADA Integration Standard; Internal Data Quality Framework

description: Total electrical energy consumed by the circuit during the period in kilowatt-hours (kWh), sourced from OSIsoft PI System metering data. Primary input for energy OPEX calculation and carbon footprint reporting.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; GRI 302-1 Energy Consumption; ISO 14001

description: Total monetary cost of electricity consumed during the period in the reporting currency, calculated as electricity_consumption_kwh multiplied by electricity_unit_cost plus applicable demand charges. Posted to SAP S/4HANA CO cost centre.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; IFRS; Internal OPEX Reporting Standard

description: Contracted or metered unit cost of electricity per kilowatt-hour ($/kWh) applicable to this period. Confidential commercial rate used for OPEX cost allocation and energy cost benchmarking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Cost Element; Utility Supply Contract; IFRS

description: Planned electrical energy consumption target for this circuit and period in kilowatt-hours (kWh), derived from the LOM plan energy budget. Used to calculate energy consumption variance for OPEX performance reporting.
reference: Internal LOM Plan; AISC Reporting Standard; ICMM Energy and GHG Protocol

description: Estimated volume of water lost to evaporation from open process vessels, ponds, and the TSF during the period in cubic metres (m³). Required for water balance closure and environmental reporting.
reference: GRI 303-5 Water Consumption; ISO 14001; Water Licence Conditions

description: Volume of fresh water drawn from licensed water sources (rivers, bores, municipal supply) into the processing plant during the period in cubic metres (m³). Reported against water licence limits for regulatory compliance.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management; GRI 303-3 Water Withdrawal; Water Licence Conditions

description: Reference identifier for the physical or virtual meter reading(s) underpinning this consumption record, as recorded in OSIsoft PI System or the utility provider invoice. Supports audit trail and data lineage for regulatory submissions.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Utility Invoice; Internal Metering Standard

description: Volume of natural gas consumed by the circuit during the period in gigajoules (GJ), used for drying, heating, or on-site power generation. Input for Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions calculation.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; GRI 302-1; NGER Act (Australia); ISO 14064

description: Free-text field for recording operational context, anomalies, meter faults, estimation methodology, or adjustment reasons relevant to this utility consumption record. Supports audit review and regulatory submissions.
Maximum instantaneous electrical power demand recorded during the period in kilowatts (kW). Used for utility tariff management, demand charge optimisation, and grid capacity planning.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Utility Tariff Agreement

description: The real-world end date and time of the utility consumption measurement period. Used with period_start_timestamp to calculate duration and validate completeness of the consumption record.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA CO Accounting Period

description: The real-world start date and time of the utility consumption measurement period. For shift records this aligns with shift start; for monthly records this is the first instant of the accounting month.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA CO Accounting Period

description: Granularity of the consumption accounting period. Shift-level records are sourced from OSIsoft PI System historian; monthly records align with SAP S/4HANA CO accounting periods for OPEX reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Controlling; OSIsoft PI System

description: Average power factor (ratio of real power to apparent power, dimensionless 0–1) for the circuit during the period. Low power factor incurs utility penalty charges and indicates reactive power inefficiency.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; Utility Tariff Agreement; IEC 60038

description: Total process water consumed within the circuit during the period (fresh intake plus recycled, minus discharge) in cubic metres (m³). Net water balance input for environmental reporting and water licence compliance.
reference: GRI 303-5 Water Consumption; ISO 14001; Water Licence Conditions

description: Current workflow lifecycle status of the utility consumption record. Draft records are pending submission; approved records are locked for OPEX and environmental reporting.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Volume of process water recycled from the Tailings Storage Facility (TSF) and other internal sources back into the processing circuit during the period in cubic metres (m³). Supports water stewardship reporting and licence compliance.
reference: GRI 303-3 Water Withdrawal; ISO 14001; Water Licence Conditions; ICMM Water Stewardship Protocol

description: Direct greenhouse gas emissions from on-site combustion of natural gas or other fuels during the period in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent (tCO₂e). Supports carbon budget compliance and NGER/GRI reporting.
reference: GRI 305-1 Direct GHG Emissions; NGER Act (Australia); ISO 14064; ICMM Climate Change Position Statement

description: Indirect greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity consumption during the period in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent (tCO₂e), calculated using applicable grid emission factors. Supports carbon budget compliance and GRI/NGER reporting.
reference: GRI 305-2 Indirect GHG Emissions; NGER Act (Australia); ISO 14064; ICMM Climate Change Position Statement

description: Electrical energy consumed per dry metric tonne of ore processed (kWh/t), calculated as electricity_consumption_kwh divided by tonnes_processed. Key comminution efficiency KPI benchmarked against LOM plan and AISC targets.
reference: ICMM Energy and GHG Protocol; Internal LOM Plan; AISC Reporting Standard

description: Process water consumed per dry metric tonne of ore processed (m³/t). Key water efficiency metric benchmarked against LOM plan targets and water licence conditions.
reference: GRI 303-5; ICMM Water Stewardship Protocol; Internal LOM Plan

description: Dry metric tonnes of ore processed through the circuit during the period. Used as the denominator for calculating specific consumption rates (e.g., kWh/t, m³/t) for benchmarking and LOM plan variance.
reference: JORC Code 2012; Internal Metallurgical Accounting Standard

description: Date and time when this utility consumption record was last modified. Tracks corrections, adjustments, and re-submissions for data lineage and audit compliance.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; ISO 14001 Audit Trail

description: Total monetary cost of fresh water intake during the period in the reporting currency, including licence fees and supply charges. Posted to SAP S/4HANA CO cost centre for OPEX tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; IFRS; Water Licence Conditions

description: Indicates whether fresh water intake during the period remained within the regulatory water licence limit (True = compliant, False = licence limit exceeded). Triggers environmental incident reporting workflow in IsoMetrix when False.
reference: ISO 14001; Water Licence Conditions; IsoMetrix HSE Incident Management

description: Regulatory water licence limit for fresh water intake applicable to this circuit and period in cubic metres (m³). Used to calculate compliance headroom and trigger licence breach alerts.
reference: Water Licence Conditions; ISO 14001; GRI 303-3; State Environmental Regulator

description: Primary key for process_area
Self-referencing FK on process_area (parent_process_area_id)
Degree of automation and control system integration for this process area.
Target mechanical availability percentage for equipment in this process area, calculated as available time divided by total time.
Reference to the processing circuit or flowsheet section this area belongs to (e.g., primary grinding circuit, rougher flotation circuit).
Externally-known unique alphanumeric code identifying the process area (e.g., SAG-01, FLOT-02, LEACH-A).
Date when the process area was commissioned and began operational service.
Type of distributed control system (DCS), programmable logic controller (PLC), or supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system managing this process area.
Financial cost center code for tracking operating expenses and capital expenditures associated with this process area.
Timestamp when this process area record was first created in the system.
Detailed textual description of the process area including its purpose, key equipment, and role in the overall processing flowsheet.
Nameplate design throughput capacity of the process area measured in tonnes per hour.
Date from which this process area configuration or record version became effective.
Date until which this process area configuration or record version remains effective, null for current records.
Regulatory environmental permit or license number authorizing operation of this process area.
Target feed particle size distribution P80 (80th percentile) in microns for material entering this process area.
Indicates whether hazardous chemicals, reagents, or materials are used or stored in this process area.
Indicates whether this process area record is currently active in the system.
Date of the most recent major capital upgrade or expansion project for this process area.
Human-readable name of the process area (e.g., Primary SAG Mill, Copper Flotation Circuit, Leach Tank Farm).
Additional operational notes, special considerations, or historical context relevant to this process area.
Planned operating hours per day for this process area, accounting for scheduled maintenance windows.
Planned decommissioning or closure date for this process area based on mine life or asset retirement plans.
Reference to the specific processing plant or concentrator facility containing this process area.
Primary mineral commodity processed in this area (e.g., iron ore, copper, coal, lithium, nickel).
Specific processing technology or method employed in this area (e.g., SAG mill, HPGR, flotation, leaching, SX-EW).
High-level classification of the process area by its primary function in the mineral processing value chain.
Target product particle size distribution P80 (80th percentile) in microns for material exiting this process area.
Reference to the employee responsible for managing operations in this process area.
Safety risk classification of the process area based on hazard assessment and potential consequence severity.
Reference to the mining site or processing plant where this process area is located.
Current operational lifecycle status of the process area.
Target concentrate or product grade for output from this process area, expressed as percentage of valuable mineral content.
Target mineral recovery rate for this process area expressed as a percentage, aligned with LOM plan targets.
Current operational target throughput for the process area in tonnes per hour, may differ from design capacity based on ore characteristics and operational strategy.
Timestamp when this process area record was last modified in the system.
Target utilization percentage for this process area, calculated as operating time divided by available time.
Unique surrogate identifier for each process parameter deviation record within the processing plant. Primary key for the process_deviation data product.
Reference to the specific processing circuit (e.g., SAG mill circuit, flotation circuit, leach circuit, SX-EW circuit) where the parameter deviation was recorded.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Asset Framework; SAP S/4HANA PM Functional Location

description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Process deviations outside control limits often require maintenance intervention to restore equipment performance (sensor calibration, actuator repair, control valve maintenance). Links process contro
Reference to the processing plant where the deviation occurred. Links to the processing_plant master record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Functional Location; OSIsoft PI System Asset Framework

description: Reference to the plant operator responsible for the circuit at the time of the deviation, used for accountability tracking and training needs analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

description: Foreign key linking to processing.shift_production_run. Business justification: Process deviations occur during a production shift run. One deviation belongs to one shift run; one shift run has many deviations. This links the deviation to the processing domain's shift entity.
Reference to the production shift during which the deviation was detected, enabling shift-level performance analysis and operator accountability.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR; Caterpillar MineStar Shift Management

description: The measured actual value of the process parameter at the time of deviation detection, as recorded by the SCADA/PI System historian or by manual operator measurement. Expressed in the unit defined by parameter_unit.
The OSIsoft PI System or SCADA tag identifier associated with the alarmed process parameter, enabling direct traceability back to the source historian record and real-time monitoring point.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Tag Naming Convention; SCADA IEC 62443

description: The specific stage within the processing circuit where the deviation occurred, such as comminution (SAG/HPGR), flotation, leaching, SX-EW, or tailings management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: comminution|classification|flotation|leaching|sxew|thickening|filtration|tailings|other — promote to reference product]
Free-text description of the corrective action taken by the operator or metallurgist to return the process parameter to within acceptable set-point tolerance, as recorded in the process control log.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; SAP S/4HANA PM Notification

description: Categorical classification of the corrective action taken, enabling aggregated analysis of response patterns and effectiveness across deviation types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: reagent_adjustment|flow_adjustment|equipment_intervention|setpoint_change|process_shutdown|no_action_required|other — promote to reference product]
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Process Control

description: Audit timestamp recording when this deviation record was first created in the system, which may differ from the detected_timestamp if the record was entered retrospectively.

The precise date and time at which the process parameter deviation was first detected, either by SCADA/PI System automated alarm or by operator observation. This is the principal real-world event time for the deviation.
Method by which the process parameter deviation was first identified, distinguishing between automated SCADA/PI System alarms and manual operator or laboratory detection.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISA-18.2 Alarm Management; LabWare LIMS

description: Indicates whether the actual parameter value exceeded the set-point (above_setpoint) or fell below it (below_setpoint), supporting directional root cause analysis and process optimisation.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

description: The absolute difference between the actual value and the set-point value (actual_value minus setpoint_value), expressed in the same engineering unit as the parameter. Positive values indicate exceedance above set-point; negative values indicate below set-point.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

description: Externally-known business reference number for the deviation event, used in corrective action reports, process control logs, and root cause analysis documentation. Format: DEV-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; OSIsoft PI System Event Frame

description: The deviation magnitude expressed as a percentage of the set-point value, enabling normalised comparison of deviation severity across parameters with different engineering units and scales.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Process Control

description: Current lifecycle state of the deviation record, tracking progression from initial detection through corrective action to closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|acknowledged|in_progress|resolved|closed|escalated — promote to reference product]
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Process Control Standards

description: Total duration in minutes for which the process parameter remained outside the acceptable control limits, from detected_timestamp to resolved_timestamp. Used for severity classification and SLA compliance assessment.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

description: Indicates whether the deviation was escalated beyond the shift operator level to the metallurgist, plant superintendent, or management due to severity, duration, or quality impact.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ISA-18.2 Alarm Management

description: SAP S/4HANA PM or Infor EAM work order number raised as a result of this deviation, where equipment failure or instrumentation fault was identified as the root cause. Enables traceability between process deviations and maintenance activities.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM; Infor EAM; ISO 55001 Asset Management

description: The minimum acceptable value for the process parameter before a deviation is triggered, as defined in the process control strategy. Expressed in the unit defined by parameter_unit.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Alarm Management; ISO 9001; ISA-18.2 Alarm Management

description: Name of the process parameter that deviated from its set-point target, such as pH, slurry density, pulp temperature, reagent flow rate, air flow rate, or feed rate. Aligns with OSIsoft PI System tag naming conventions.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Tag Naming; SCADA IEC 62443; ISO 9001

description: Categorical classification of the process parameter type that deviated, enabling aggregated analysis by parameter category across circuits and plants. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pH|density|temperature|flow_rate|pressure|level|speed|grade|reagent_dosage|other — promote to reference product]
reference: OSIsoft PI System; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

description: Engineering unit of measure for the process parameter (e.g., pH units, g/cm³, °C, m³/h, kPa, rpm, g/t). Required for correct interpretation of set-point, actual, and deviation magnitude values.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Engineering Units; ISO 80000 Quantities and Units

business_glossary_term: OSIsoft PI System Event Frame ID
description: The unique event frame identifier from the OSIsoft PI System historian that corresponds to this deviation record, enabling direct cross-reference to the source process data historian for detailed time-series analysis.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Event Frame; SCADA IEC 62443

description: Estimated tonnes of concentrate or processed ore lost due to the deviation, as assessed by the metallurgist. Used for OPEX impact quantification and LOM plan variance reporting.
reference: JORC Code; SAP S/4HANA CO; ICMM Mineral Processing

description: Indicates whether the process parameter deviation had a measurable impact on product quality (concentrate grade, recovery rate, or product specification compliance). True if quality impact was confirmed.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; JORC Code; ICMM

description: Estimated percentage point impact on metallurgical recovery rate attributable to this deviation, as assessed by the metallurgist. Negative values indicate recovery loss. Null if no recovery impact was identified.
reference: JORC Code; ICMM Mineral Processing; ISO 9001

description: Indicates whether this deviation is a recurrence of a previously recorded deviation for the same parameter and circuit within a defined lookback period, flagging chronic process control issues for targeted investigation.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Continuous Improvement

description: Date and time at which the process parameter was returned to within acceptable set-point tolerance and the deviation was formally resolved. Null if deviation is still open.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; OSIsoft PI System

description: High-level categorisation of the identified root cause of the deviation, used for trend analysis, recurring deviation identification, and process improvement initiatives. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|feed_variability|reagent_issue|operator_error|instrumentation_fault|utility_disruption|process_upset|unknown — promote to reference product]
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Process Safety; IsoMetrix

description: Detailed free-text description of the identified root cause of the process deviation, as determined through investigation by the metallurgist or process engineer. Supports root cause analysis (RCA) and continuous improvement.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; ICMM Process Safety

description: The target or nominal set-point value for the process parameter as defined in the process control strategy or standard operating procedure (SOP). Expressed in the unit defined by parameter_unit.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SAP S/4HANA PP; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

description: Categorical severity classification of the deviation based on magnitude, duration, and potential impact on product quality, recovery rate, or plant safety. Drives escalation and corrective action urgency.
reference: ISA-18.2 Alarm Management; ISO 9001; ICMM Process Safety

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this deviation record originated, supporting data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking. Values include OSIsoft PI System, SCADA, manual entry, LabWare LIMS, or MES.
reference: OSIsoft PI System; SCADA IEC 62443; LabWare LIMS

description: Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this deviation record, used for data lineage and change tracking in the Silver layer.
The maximum acceptable value for the process parameter before a deviation is triggered, as defined in the process control strategy. Expressed in the unit defined by parameter_unit.
reference: OSIsoft PI System Alarm Management; ISO 9001; ISA-18.2 Alarm Management

Critical rating indicates stakeholder opposition could halt operations, high indicates significant project delays possible, medium indicates manageable concerns, low indicates supportive or neutral stance.
reference: ICMM Social Licence to Operate Framework

description: Hierarchical classification based on proximity to operations and impact level. Primary stakeholders are directly affected by mining activities, secondary are indirectly affected, key stakeholders have significant influence, tertiary have minimal direct impact.
Full legal or registered name of the stakeholder entity or individual. For indigenous groups, traditional community names. For NGOs and government bodies, official registered name.

Primary classification of the stakeholder entity. Distinguishes between local communities, indigenous groups, individual landowners, non-governmental organisations, government bodies, and advocacy organisations.

Indicates whether the stakeholder holds traditional ownership or native title rights over land affected by mining operations. Used to identify parties requiring specific consultation and consent protocols.

Foreign key linking to the Life of Mine plan being consulted on

Reference identifier to any formal agreement, memorandum of understanding, or consent document resulting from this consultation (e.g., land use agreement number, benefit sharing agreement ID).

Name or identifier of the company representative or team who conducted this consultation. Used for accountability and follow-up.
The date on which formal consultation with this stakeholder regarding this LOM plan occurred. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and social licence tracking.
Free-text summary of the consultation outcome, including key concerns raised, commitments made, and any conditions attached to stakeholder support.
System timestamp when this consultation record was created in the data platform.
The mine lifecycle phase during which this consultation occurred. Critical for tracking consultation requirements across different regulatory and planning stages.
The date by which follow-up consultation with this stakeholder on this LOM plan is required, based on regulatory requirements or agreement terms.
The method used to notify and engage this stakeholder about this LOM plan. Must align with stakeholder's preferred communication channel and cultural considerations.
Indicates whether this consultation satisfied applicable regulatory requirements for stakeholder engagement (e.g., Environmental Impact Assessment consultation requirements).
System timestamp when this consultation record was last updated.

Reference to the parent stakeholder organisation or community group this contact person is affiliated with.

Unique identifier for the credit limit record. Primary key for the credit limit entity.
Reference to the commodity buyer, offtake counterparty, or trading partner to whom this credit limit is assigned. Links to the customer master data.

Name or title of the individual, committee, or governance body that approved this credit limit. Examples include Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Credit Committee, Board of Directors, or Regional Credit Manager. Provides audit trail for credit limit authorization.
Date on which the credit limit was formally approved by the designated approval authority. Establishes the authorization date for audit and compliance purposes.
Remaining credit capacity available for new transactions. Calculated as limit_amount minus utilisation_amount. Negative values indicate over-limit exposure requiring management intervention.

Value of the collateral or credit enhancement securing this credit limit. Typically expressed in the same currency as the credit limit. For parent guarantees this may be the guaranteed amount, for standby LCs this is the LC face value.

Reference number or identifier for the collateral instrument securing this credit limit. For standby LCs this is the LC number, for guarantees this is the guarantee reference, for cash deposits this is the deposit account reference.

Type of credit enhancement or collateral arrangement securing the credit limit. Parent guarantees are common for subsidiary buyers, standby letters of credit (LC) provide bank-backed security, cash deposits are held as security, bank guarantees are issued by financial institutions, insurance bonds are provided by credit insurers, and asset pledges involve physical or financial assets as security. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|parent_guarantee|standby_lc|cash_deposit|bank_guarantee|insurance_bond|asset_pledge — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Date and time when this credit limit record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for record creation.
Business identifier for the credit limit agreement. Externally visible reference number used in credit management communications and approvals.

Current lifecycle status of the credit limit. Draft limits are being prepared, pending approval limits await credit committee authorization, active limits are in force, suspended limits are temporarily blocked due to payment issues or risk concerns, expired limits have passed their validity date, cancelled limits have been terminated, and under review limits are being reassessed due to changed circumstances. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|active|suspended|expired|cancelled|under_review — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Classification of the credit limit based on its purpose and duration. Master limits are ongoing, temporary limits are short-term extensions, project-specific limits are tied to individual mining projects or shipments, seasonal limits accommodate cyclical demand, spot trade limits cover one-off transactions, and offtake agreement limits are tied to long-term supply contracts.

External or internal credit rating assigned to the counterparty that forms the basis for the credit limit determination. Ratings follow standard agency notation (AAA highest, D default, NR not rated). May be sourced from agencies like Moody's, S&P, Fitch, or internal credit risk models. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: AAA|AA|A|BBB|BB|B|CCC|CC|C|D|NR — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Name of the credit rating agency or internal risk assessment team that provided the credit rating. Examples include Moody's, Standard & Poor's, Fitch Ratings, or Internal Credit Risk Committee.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the credit limit is denominated. Common currencies for mining commodity trading include USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, and AUD.

Number of days from invoice date within which payment must be received to qualify for the early payment discount. Typically shorter than the full payment terms (e.g., 10 days for discount vs 30 days net).

Percentage discount offered to the customer for early payment within a specified discount period. For example, 2% discount if paid within 10 days (2/10 net 30 terms). Incentivizes prompt payment and reduces Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
Date from which the credit limit becomes active and enforceable. Shipments and invoices on or after this date are subject to this credit limit.
Date on which the credit limit ceases to be valid. Nullable for open-ended master limits that remain in force until explicitly revised or cancelled.

Percentage of the credit limit covered by credit insurance. Typically ranges from 80% to 95%, with the mining company retaining a deductible or co-insurance portion to align incentives for credit risk management.

Reference number for the credit insurance policy covering this counterparty exposure, if applicable. Credit insurance protects against non-payment risk and is common for high-value or high-risk commodity trading relationships.
Date of the most recent periodic review of this credit limit. Updated each time the credit limit undergoes scheduled or ad-hoc reassessment by the credit risk team.

Annual percentage rate charged on overdue balances as a penalty for late payment. Applied to the outstanding amount for each day or month beyond the payment due date. Helps enforce payment discipline and compensates for financing costs.

Maximum approved credit exposure amount that the counterparty is authorized to utilize. Represents the total outstanding receivables (invoiced but unpaid) that the customer may accumulate before further shipments are blocked.
Date and time when this credit limit record was last modified. Updated whenever any attribute of the credit limit is changed, supporting change tracking and audit requirements.
Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this credit limit. Calculated based on the last review date plus the review frequency. Triggers workflow notifications to credit risk analysts.

Free-text field for additional context, special conditions, or commentary related to this credit limit. May include details on negotiation history, special approval conditions, temporary adjustments, or risk mitigation measures.

Primary payment instrument or mechanism agreed for settlement of invoices under this credit limit. Telegraphic transfer (TT) is direct bank wire, letter of credit (LC) provides bank-backed payment assurance, documentary collection involves bank-mediated document exchange, cash against documents (CAD) requires payment before document release, open account allows payment after delivery, and advance payment requires prepayment before shipment.

Standard number of days from Bill of Lading (B/L) date or invoice date within which payment is due. Common terms in commodity trading include 30, 60, 90, or 120 days. Aligned with the offtake agreement or sales contract payment terms.

Number of months between scheduled reviews of this credit limit. High-risk counterparties may be reviewed quarterly (3 months), standard counterparties semi-annually (6 months), and low-risk counterparties annually (12 months). Ensures credit limits remain aligned with counterparty creditworthiness.

Internal risk category assigned to the counterparty based on credit assessment, payment history, financial health, and market conditions. Low risk counterparties have strong financials and payment track record, medium risk have acceptable credit profiles, high risk require enhanced monitoring, watch list indicates deteriorating conditions, and default indicates payment failure or insolvency.

Current outstanding receivables balance against this credit limit. Calculated in real-time as the sum of all unpaid invoices and open deliveries. When utilisation approaches or exceeds the limit amount, shipment blocks are triggered.

reference: World Gold Council AISC Standard; IFRS IAS 21 Foreign Currency; SAP S/4HANA CO

description: Calculated per-unit AISC or C1 cash cost expressed in USD per production unit of measure (e.g., USD/oz for gold, USD/lb for copper, USD/dmt for iron ore). reference: World Gold Council AISC Standard; Brook Hunt C1 Framework; SEC S-K 1300

description: Date and time when this cost performance report record was last modified. Tracks restatements, corrections, or updates to cost components following period-end close adjustments in SAP CO.

description: Percentage variance of actual unit cost result against the budget unit cost for the period. Positive values indicate cost overrun; negative values indicate cost underperformance. Calculated as ((unit_cost_result - budget_unit_cost) / budget_unit_cost) * 100.

description: Percentage variance of actual unit cost result against the prior period unit cost. Used in quarterly investor reports and management commentary to explain cost movement drivers.
reference: World Gold Council AISC Standard; ASX Listing Rules; SEC S-K 1300

Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation for the asset. Mining assets commonly use 'units_of_production' (UOP) aligned to ore reserve depletion or 'straight_line' over useful life. Corresponds to SAP depreciation key configuration.
